title: Functional limit theorems for weighted occupation times of supercritical superprocesses
abstract: Suppose $X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a supercritical superprocess with a non-local branching mechanism on a Lusin space $E$, whose mean semigroup admits a positive leading eigenvalue $λ_1$ with a bounded positive eigenfunction $\varphi$ and a finite eigenmeasure $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Let $Y_t:=\int_0^t X_s\mathrm{d}s$ be its occupation measure. We first prove a law of large numbers, that is, for every bounded measurable function $f$, $e^{-λ_1 t}\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ converges in $L^2$ to $λ_1^{-1}\langle f,\widetilde{\varphi}\rangle W^\varphi_\infty$, where $W^\varphi_\infty$ is the limit of the martingale $W^\varphi_t:=e^{-λ_1 t}\langle\varphi,X_t\rangle$. We then establish functional central limit theorems for the fluctuations of $\langle f,Y_t\rangle$ around this random centering. We show that the normalisation and the limit are determined by the spectral decay rate of $f$ compared with the critical value $λ_1/2$, and there are three possible regimes: after suitable normalisation, the fluctuation process converges in distribution in $\mathcal{C}[0,+\infty)$ either to a mixed Gaussian process $\sqrt{W^{\varphi}_{\infty}}G(f)$, or to a constant Gaussian process with random variance depending on $W^{\varphi}_{\infty}$, or to a non-Gaussian limit given by the limit of a martingale associated with the spectral projection of $f$. These results are the occupation-time counterparts of the fluctuation theorems for linear functionals of supercritical non-local branching superprocesses.

title: Kobayashi visibility of strictly convex domains
abstract: We show that any bounded strictly convex domain in $\Bbb C^N$, endowed with the Kobayashi distance, is visible.

title: A proof of Borcea's quadratic variance conjecture
abstract: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n\ge2$, and let $σ_2(p)$ be the root mean square distance of its zeros from their centroid, including multiplicities. We prove that every zero of $p$ lies within distance $σ_2(p)$ of a critical point. This proves Borcea's quadratic conjecture and, in particular, gives a new proof of Sendov's conjecture. Two polynomial integration identities prove the result analytically for $n\ge2048$. For the remaining degrees, we derive explicit necessary inequalities, including a variable integration endpoint and an exact centered coefficient identity. Directed integer arithmetic certifies a finite covering of the resulting parameter domains. Degrees $4$--$26$ use $150\,845$ certified three-dimensional regions; degrees $27$--$2047$ use a further $27\,429$ regions, with degree intervals allowed. The cases of degree 2 and 3 were already covered by Khavinson--Pereira--Putinar--Saff--Shimorin.

title: The six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based
abstract: We show that the six-element additively idempotent semiring $B_2^1$ is inherently nonfinitely based. More precisely, for every positive integer $n$, we construct an infinite additively idempotent semiring, generated by at most $(6n+8)^2$ elements, that satisfies every $n$-variable identity of $B_2^1$.

title: Hölder Continuity and Boundedness of Composition Operators on Pluriharmonic $α$-Bloch Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study the metric properties of pluriharmonic $α$-Bloch-type mappings $f=h+\overline{g}\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{B}^{n},\mathbb{C}^{n})$ on the unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n}\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$. By synthesizing local real-part estimates with the subharmonicity of $\log(\vert{} \det Dh(z) \vert{} + \vert{} \det Dg(z) \vert{})$ along hyperbolic geodesics, we establish a globalized non-trivial lower bound across the entire unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n}$. Using this structural decay estimate, we prove that the invariant weight quantity $D_{f}^{n,α}(z)$ satisfies a global Hölder continuity estimate of order $1/n$ with respect to the Bergman metric $β$. Furthermore, we investigate composition operators $C_{\varphi}(f)=f\circ\varphi$ induced by holomorphic self-mappings $\varphi\in\mathcal{A}(\mathbb{B}^{n},\mathbb{B}^{n})$. We establish both sharp sufficient and necessary sampling conditions for $C_{\varphi}$ to be bounded from below on the pluriharmonic $α$-Bloch space $\mathcal{B}_{P(n,α)}$.

title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
abstract:
We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erdős-Rényi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$.
  For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

title: Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three
abstract: We prove that every finite ordered set of width at most three and cardinality at least four is reconstructible from its deck. This settles the width-three part of an open problem posed by Schröder in Ordered Sets; the separate question concerning ordered sets of height one is not addressed here. The new ingredient is a criterion for recovering the marked maximal deck of an ordered set with exactly three maximal elements from its unmarked maximal deck and the isomorphism type of the suborder obtained by deleting all maximal elements. We express the criterion as an orbital balance condition on the attachment ideals in this common base. Necessity follows by double counting; sufficiency uses the structure of automorphism actions in width at most three. The full-deck theorem then follows from reconstruction results of Schröder concerning maximal cards and marked maximal cards. A local reattachment argument correcting one intermediate step in the two-maximal-element case is included in an appendix.

title: A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations
abstract: The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.

title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.

title: Stochastic Modelling of Telomere Length Dynamics During Hematopoiesis
abstract: We introduce a new stochastic model of telomere length dynamics during hematopoiesis. The numerous cell divisions occurring in this setting makes telomere length dynamics, and in particular their attrition, a crucial aspect of hematopoiesis. After recalling the main aspect of the biological setting, we describe an individual based model of hematopoietic population cells. We then study its behaviour in the large population limit, as well as its fluctuations.

title: Equality Cases in the Tu-Deng Conjecture Bound
abstract:
The Tu-Deng Conjecture, made in 2011, asserts that for $k\geq2$ and $1\leq t<2^k-1$, the set \[ S_{t,k}=\left\{(a,b)\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^k-2\}^2:
  a+b\equiv t\pmod{2^k-1},\quad \wt(a)+\wt(b)<k\right\} \] satisfies \[
  |S_{t,k}|\leq 2^{k-1}. \] Proofs of the conjecture were given independently by the author and by Liu, Luo and Xie in arXiv in 2026. Let $r=\wt(t)$, and let $z=k-r$ be the number of zeros in the $k$-bit expansion of $t$. We prove that equality holds in the Tu-Deng Conjecture if and only if every cyclic distance between consecutive zeros is at least $z$. We give several other simple necessary and sufficient conditions, including a forbidden-pattern condition, a packing condition for the zero positions, a composition condition for the gaps, and equivalent conditions involving the coefficients of the polynomial $H_W(u,v)$ in the proof of the Tu-Deng conjecture. We also count the equality words having a prescribed number of zeros.

title: Removing Boundary Smoothness from the Hot-Spots Conclusion in the Simple-Eigenvalue Case
abstract: We give a reduction from a smooth-domain theorem excluding interior critical points of first positive Neumann eigenfunctions to a non-strict hot-spots conclusion on arbitrary bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple first positive eigenvalue. The main analytic step is spectral convergence under exhaustion by conformal images of concentric disks. A reflection extension, conformal invariance of Dirichlet energy, and compactness of the Sobolev embedding give a direct proof. A truncation argument justifies square integrability of the transferred extensions without any boundary regularity. The smooth-domain theorem proved by OpenAI is an external input; the approximation argument is proved here in full. The paper was generated by ChatGPT with prompts from the listed author.

title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.

title: LInearity of Tubular Groups
abstract: We prove that a tubular group is linear if and only if it is residually finite, equivalently virtually primitive. Every such group embeds in $\SL_n(\Z[u])$. For a primitive tubular decomposition with at most $m$ edge slopes at each vertex, our representation has dimension $2\max\{2,m\}$. In particular, Gersten's group embeds in $\SL_6(\Z[u])$, and this dimension is minimal.

title: A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem
abstract: In this note we show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. Combined with an announced result of Auroux, Bai and Pomerleano, this shows that for some $4 \le n \le 8$ there is a complex affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative.

title: Quaternion Gaussian Probes for Tensor Frobenius-Norm Estimation
abstract: Large-scale tensors arising in science and engineering are often too large to form or store explicitly. Their multilinear contractions, however, can frequently be evaluated efficiently, which makes randomized Frobenius-norm estimation a practical alternative to exact computation. In this paper, we study estimation of the squared Frobenius norm of a real order-$d$ tensor from such contractions using independent real, complex, or quaternion Gaussian probes. For a rank-one tensor, one normalized sample is a product of $d-1$ independent Gamma variables. This gives exact relative-variance factors $3^{d-1}-1$, $2^{d-1}-1$, and $(3/2)^{d-1}-1$, respectively. Under the same budget of underlying real Gaussian vectors, the quaternion probe has smaller rank-one variance than four independent real probes for $d\ge3$; a real-channel representation identifies the gain as modewise pooling. For orthogonal CP tensors, the exact relative variance equals the corresponding rank-one factor divided by the participation-ratio effective rank and the number of samples. For arbitrary real tensors, we prove sharp uniform moment bounds, attained at rank one, and obtain Chebyshev guarantees. A classical block-median construction then gives two-sided exponential confidence for the modified estimator. Numerical examples test the rank-one and effective-rank formulas. An implicit infinite-series kernel tensor illustrates contraction-based norm evaluation; EEG maps provide a qualitative spatial interpolation illustration.

title: Geometric operators and the third problem of Halmos
abstract: In 1970, P. R. Halmos raised ten open problems on operator theory. The third problem of Halmos is the following: if an intransitive operator has an inverse, is its inverse also intransitive? This question is reduced to the case of conjugate bi-geometric operators in arXiv: 2610.11202. In the framework of conjugate bi-geometric operators, using tools from complex geometry, operator theory, and function theory, this paper gives an affirmative answer to the third problem of Halmos in the following cases: (a) bundle-preserving operator;(b) subexponential growth of operator norms. These two cases cover a large class of operators.

title: Quantitative spectral stability and sharp Fourier estimates for periodic CMV matrices with decaying perturbations
abstract: We study half-line CMV matrices whose Verblunsky coefficients are decaying perturbations of periodic sequences. We quantify the stability of fine properties of the absolutely continuous spectral measure under such perturbations. More precisely, we establish Hölder continuity of the perturbed spectral measure and derive sharp time-averaged Fourier estimates governing the associated quantum dynamics. These results remain valid up to the edges of the absolutely continuous spectrum. Since the spectral measure of a half-line CMV matrix is precisely the orthogonality measure for the corresponding orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle (OPUC), our results also yield new statements for OPUC whose Verblunsky coefficients are decaying perturbations of periodic sequences.

title: Quasipositive Braids, Presentations, and Garside Structures
abstract: We provide a presentation of the braid group in which the generating set is the set of all positive half-twists, the relations are balanced positive relations, and every relation is conjugate to one in a finite list. We then prove that for any such presentation, its positive monoid is not isomorphic to the quasipositive braid monoid. Finally, we show that the quasipositive braid monoid has no proper Garside family. These results settle a problem of Calegari from the K3 problems list.

title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
abstract: We establish a Carathéodory-type extension theorem for premeasures with values in general separated abelian net convergence groups. Starting from hereditary exhaustivity on the source ring and intrinsic conditions for combining null errors, we construct a countably additive extension on a regulated Boolean sigma-algebra, with full upper and lower regularity in the original convergence. Completeness is required only on the limit-stable hull of the source range. Under closed summation for arbitrary directed rows and finite-response reflection, we identify the regulated domain with the splitting class of Sion's inner and outer processes. For a Dedekind-complete real vector lattice, we show that sequential closed summation on a bounded interval is equivalent to weak sigma-distributivity of the generated band, giving a converge-theoretic interpretation of the concept. Source representations allow us to recover the partially ordered-group extension of Volauf and the finite-variation extension of Kusraev and Malyugin from the general theorem. We then treat finite semivariation by adjoining dominated coordinate variations to an additive lift of the premeasure. The resulting extension is defined on the full semivariation regulator domain and preserves semivariation exactly, without requiring decomposability or the countable sup property. It includes measures of infinite vector variation.

title: Reflexivity of Grothendieck Spaces and Strongly Normal Sequences
abstract: A normalized sequence $(y_n)$ in the dual $E^{*}$ of a Banach space $E$ is called normal if it is weak-star null, and strongly normal if [ G(y_n)=\left{x\in E:\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n(x)|<\infty\right} ] is dense in $E$. We prove that, within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, reflexivity is characterized by the subsequence behavior of normal sequences: a Grothendieck space $E$ is reflexive if and only if every normal sequence in $E^{*}$ contains a strongly normal subsequence. If $E$ is nonreflexive and Grothendieck, then $E^{*}$ contains a normalized weakly null sequence none of whose subsequences is strongly normal; more strongly, it contains a closed hereditarily $\ell_{1}$ subspace $Y$ with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis such that no sequence in $S(Y)$ is strongly normal. We also obtain an exact quotient criterion valid for arbitrary Banach spaces: a normal sequence has a strongly normal subsequence precisely when, for some subsequence $z=(z_n)$, the quotient $E/\bigcap_n\ker z_n$ is separable. The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson--Maurey--Schechtman and Popov. Concrete realizations are given in $(L_{\infty}(μ))^{*}$ for nonatomic probability spaces (and, more generally, for $σ$-finite spaces with a nonatomic part) and in $\ell_{\infty}^{*}$.

title: Global Well-Posedness and Energy Decay for an Abstract Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlocal or Friction Damping
abstract: This paper investigates an abstract viscoelastic wave equation in a separable Hilbert space, in which the damping term depends on a power of the velocity norm. Depending on whether the power exponent is zero or nonzero, this damping corresponds to friction damping or nonlocal damping, respectively; the equation also contains a viscoelastic damping represented by an integral term with a relaxation function. We establish global well-posedness for initial data in \(\mathcal{H}_1\) by combining monotone operator theory with the Faedo--Galerkin method, and prove uniqueness for all exponents greater than \(-1\), with the singular range between \(-1\) and \(0\) handled through the monotonicity rather than the Lipschitz continuity of the nonlocal damping operator. We then study the long-time behavior of the energy via integral inequalities, multiplier techniques, and Nakao's method, and obtain explicit decay estimates showing that the energy decays exponentially in the friction case and polynomially in the nonlocal case. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to consider the combined effects of viscoelastic damping and nonlocal damping in such an abstract framework, and it is also the first to analyze nonlocal damping with negative exponents.

title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.

title: Compact Mean Curvature Flows from Non-Compact Initial Data
abstract: We construct compact, embedded solutions to the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that arise from various non-compact initial data and exist for a finite time.

title: Large deviations for additive functionals of one-dimensional zero-range processes
abstract: We prove a large deviation principle for additive functionals of local Lipschitz functions of a one-dimensional symmetric zero-range process on the diffusive scale. The rate function is obtained from the dynamical large deviation principle for the empirical density and is characterized by a variational constraint involving the density at a fixed spatial point. On the microscopic side, a super-exponential replacement is needed to replace the local observable with a function of the empirical density. On the macroscopic side, the spatial regularity enjoyed by finite-rate trajectories is needed to pass from spatial averages to point evaluation.

title: Stability threshold of the Couette flow in 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations on $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$
abstract:
In this paper, we study the transition threshold problem for the 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations around the Couette flow with a constant background temperature in two domains: $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$.
  It was proved that if the sizes of initial perturbations of the vorticity and the temperature in Sobolev spaces are $ν^{\fr13}$ and $ν^{\fr56}$, respectively, then this system admits a globally stable solution.
  Besides, we derive the enhanced dissipation estimate for the vorticity and temperature, as well as the inviscid damping estimate for the velocity. The coupling in the equations poses some difficulties to the analysis. We overcome these challenges and establish the results via the quasi-linear method and energy estimates.

title: A Sklar-Type Decomposition for Positive Binary Distributions and a Gibbs Interpretation
abstract: We study strictly positive multivariate binary distributions by separating one-body marginals from dependence. Local positive reweighting defines a dependence nucleus, completely characterized by the higher-order Walsh log-linear coefficients $J_S$, $|S|\ge2$. Any such nucleus and any strictly positive one-body marginals determine a unique joint distribution. In finite-spin Gibbs systems, these coefficients are the many-body interaction couplings.

title: Chern classes of Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds
abstract: We construct closed Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds with non-vanishing Chern monomials. For every $n \geq 2$ and $\lceil n / 4 \rceil \leq m \leq \lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$, there exists a $(2 n + 1)$-dimensional example of signature $(\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor, \lceil n / 2 \rceil)$ on which all Chern monomials with positive indices at most $m$ and total weight at most $n - m$ are non-zero in cohomology with real coefficients. Taking $m = \lceil n / 4 \rceil$ gives examples with $c_{1}^{\lfloor 3 n / 4 \rfloor} \neq 0$. For $n = 4$ or $n \geq 6$, the latter examples show that the Chern-class vanishing theorem for strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds does not extend to the Levi non-degenerate case. In these dimensions, their underlying manifolds admit no strictly pseudoconvex CR structures. The construction uses circle bundles over products of integral pseudo-Kähler manifolds.

title: Wiener's lemma for quasicrystals: hull-uniform decay of covariant kernels on Delone sets
abstract:
This paper studies continuous covariant kernel families over hulls of Delone sets of finite local complexity using graded Wiener-algebra methods. The norm given by the least common weighted summable off-diagonal profile is identified isometrically with a graded $\ell^1$-norm. The resulting Banach $*$-algebras are symmetric, spectrally invariant in the reduced groupoid C*-algebra, and stable under holomorphic functional calculus. Exact physical weights give preservation of polynomial and stretched-exponential classes, including a fixed stretched-exponential rate.
  A configuration with dense orbit has a faithful regular representation. Invertibility on that configuration therefore gives an inverse family with one profile valid throughout the hull; for repetitive sets every configuration has this property.
  For polynomial weights of order $s>0$, return-vector counting yields a differential estimate with parameter $κ/(κ+s)$, where $κ$ is a growth exponent of the return vectors and may be taken equal to $d$ for Meyer sets. Combined with established norm-controlled inversion criteria, this gives explicit bounds in the common-profile norm. Explicit bounds are also obtained for stretched-exponential physical weights and for gapped Fermi projections.

title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: An elementary approach to the Szegő theorems
abstract: The strong Szegő theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. In particular, Szegő's theorem states that, beyond the leading extensive contribution to such a determinant, there is a universal finite correction, $\sum_{r>0} rV_rV_{-r}$ where $V_r$ are the Fourier coefficients of the logarithm of the symbol. Although this formula appears throughout analysis and mathematical physics, the origin of its quadratic form and of the weight $r$ is often obscured in its standard analytic derivations. We develop an elementary picture in which the strong Szegő term arises from boundary leakage: paths contributing to the matrix exponential leave the finite interval and subsequently return. Counting the shortest such excursions immediately produces the factor $r$. We then show that an isolated boundary contributes exactly one half of the strong Szegő correction, while the two boundaries of a long interval decouple. For finite-range matrices this gives a rigorous and intuitive elementary derivation of the asymptotics, with extensions to sufficiently rapidly decaying interactions. A complementary free-fermion argument provides a physical interpretation of the same cancellation mechanism. Numerical examples illustrate the asymtotics in the well controlled regime, the Fisher Hartwig logarithmic correction. The boundary formulation does not itself require translation invariance and therefore suggests natural extensions to disordered systems, higher dimensions, and symbols with internal matrix structure. To illustrate this we numerically go beyond the formal applicability region of the Szegő formula, considering slow decay and disordered cases, and showing in some cases a robustness of the approach even for slowly decaying but disordered potentials.

title: The Stable Marriage Polytope is Box-Totally Dual Integral
abstract: A stable matching in a bipartite preference system is a matching that has no unmatched pair whose endpoints both prefer each other to their current assignments. Rothblum gave a linear description of the stable marriage polytope, the convex hull of the incidence vectors of stable matchings. We prove that this polytope is box-totally dual integral. The proof uses the affine representation of the stable marriage polytope as an order polytope together with the matricial characterization of box-TDI polyhedra. Since Kiraly and Pap proved that Rothblum's description is totally dual integral, our result further implies that Rothblum's system is box-totally dual integral.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.

title: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
abstract: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.

title: The square function estimate for the cone in four dimensions
abstract: We obtain the $L^3$ reverse square function estimate for the light cone in four dimensions from the critical local-smoothing and round-cone propagation statements in the September 2026 OpenAI manuscript. We state these inputs, together with the plate maximal theorem of Di Plinio and Parissis, in a preliminaries section. The proof passes from geometric concentration of packet coefficients to regularity of the analyzed wave, and then from free waves to arbitrary functions supported near the cone. As a consequence, we obtain the corresponding $L^3$ estimate for the sphere and elliptic paraboloids in three dimensions.

title: Optimal Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities under different relaxations of bounded variance assumption
abstract: We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with $m$ workers, $K$ oracle calls per worker per round, and $N$ rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from $(KN)^{-1/2}$ to $(KN)^{-1}$ with local steps and from $(mKN)^{-1/2}$ to $(mKN)^{-1}$ with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in $m$. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over $KN$ sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all $mKN$ samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an $N^{-2}$ gradient term, a $(KN)^{-1}$ monotone term, and a $(mKN)^{-1}$ sampling term, without assuming SGC.

title: Lusztig Parameters and Factorizations of Determinantial Modules
abstract: We give an explicit formula for the Lusztig parameters of determinantial modules over symmetric quiver Hecke algebras. The formula applies to every Bruhat pair and every fixed reduced expression of the upper Weyl group element. In finite types $A$, $D$, and $E$, we identify the parameters of the modules in Ménard's seed using Demazure weaves. We then factor prefix determinantial modules into these seed modules, with multiplicities given by Lusztig cycles. We also give a criterion for recognizing monomials in this fixed seed and an explicit formula recovering their multiplicities from Lusztig parameters.

title: On the Five-Point Case of Mordell's Problem
abstract: For five complex points $z_1,\ldots,z_5$ satisfying $\sum_i|z_i|^2=5$, Mordell's discriminant inequality states that $\prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^2\leq5^5$, with equality precisely for a unit regular pentagon, up to rotation and permutation. We organize its proof around a direct comparison of discriminant values. A global maximizer gives a centered stationary configuration, whose coefficient equations reduce the generic case to two quartic branches. On each branch, the absolute value of a cubic polynomial gives the original discriminant objective after accounting for the normalization scale. Exact rational interval bounds exclude both branches from the maximum, and the exceptional coefficient cases leave the regular pentagon. The argument determines the maximizing configuration without reconstructing all stationary shapes. We have completed a full Lean formalization of the five-point inequality and both directions of its equality condition, including all reductions and finite checks used in this proof.

title: Singular Levi-flats and holomorphic foliations on projective spaces
abstract: We study codimension-one holomorphic foliations admitting invariant singular real-analytic Levi-flat varieties. Our main problem is to determine when the local meromorphic first integrals furnished by the Levi-flat geometry can be continued coherently and globalized. We introduce a pencil-singularity condition and a projective compatibility condition for local meromorphic parameters. In the projective plane these yield a characterization of foliations admitting a primitive rational first integral, while in higher-dimensional projective space they give a rational integrability criterion under a generic local-product hypothesis along the dicritical locus. We also obtain semi-global and Stein versions of these results. In a different direction, we study foliations admitting infinitely many invariant Levi-flat varieties and prove a Darboux-type alternative: either the foliation admits a rational first integral, or infinitely many Levi-flats contain a common invariant algebraic curve whose virtual holonomy is abelian. Under additional assumptions on the singularities, this leads to the existence of a closed rational, and in the absence of saddle-nodes a closed logarithmic, defining \(1\)-form.

title: Generating Sets for the Kernels of Frobenius Polarization Operators
abstract: We study generating sets for the kernels of the Frobenius polarization operators associated with elements of finite groups. By applying the discrete Fourier transform on each coset, we describe these kernels in terms of additive semigroups defined by zero-sum relations among roots of unity. We show that the monomials corresponding to the minimal nonzero elements of these semigroups form generating sets of minimum cardinality. We further describe the minimal nonzero elements in the general case in terms of those in the cyclic case and obtain a formula for the minimum number of generators. For the operator associated with a generator of a cyclic group, we also show, as a consequence of known results on integer zero-sum relations and circulant determinant representations, that its kernel and the subalgebra generated by these circulant determinants have the same field of fractions.

title: Homogeneous symmetric trace-positive sextics with vanishing abelianization are sums of Hermitian squares and commutators
abstract: Let $\mathbb{R}\langle X,Y\rangle$ be the free algebra on two symmetric letters. A polynomial is trace-positive if it has non-negative trace on every pair of real symmetric matrices, and it lies in the cone $Θ$ if it is cyclically equivalent to a sum of Hermitian squares. Burgdorf and Klep proved that the two notions coincide in degree at most four; from degree six onwards they differ. We give a complete, explicit description of both cones on the six-dimensional space $Z$ of symmetric homogeneous sextics in two symmetric letters whose abelianization vanishes identically, and show that on $Z$ they coincide: for $f\in Z$, trace-positivity is equivalent to membership in $Θ_3$, to non-negativity of the trace on pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices, and to being cyclically equivalent to a sum of four Hermitian squares of cubics with vanishing abelianization. Membership in $Θ$ reduces to a $4\times4$ positive semidefinite Gram matrix whose diagonal blocks are fixed by the content-$(4,2)$ and $(2,4)$ parts of $f$; each of those parts ranges over a two-dimensional cone with two linear facets, and the content-$(3,3)$ part is then confined to a rectangle whose sides are the geometric means $\sqrt{p_+q_+}$ and $\sqrt{p_-q_-}$ of the eigenvalues of those blocks. Each facet is certified by one of two families of pairs of $2\times2$ symmetric matrices. The abelianization hypothesis is natural: every bivariate degree-six example we are aware of -- a trace-positive polynomial outside $Θ$ -- arises by lifting a non-negative, non-SOS polynomial in two variables to a cyclically sorted polynomial; and that lifting cannot operate when the abelianization vanishes. Symmetry of $f$ is essential: dropping it adds one antisymmetric direction, on which the trace vanishes identically, yet whose non-zero elements all lie outside $Θ$.

title: On the non-existence of a left-symmetric structure on osp(1|2) in any characteristic
abstract: Burde proved that the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of characteristic $p > 2$, admits compatible left-symmetric algebra structures if and only if $p = 3$. Since the even part of the Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, we ask whether Burde's structures can be extended to compatible left-symmetric superalgebra structures on $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$. We verify Burde's left-symmetric structures on $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{K})$, and then test their possible extensions to $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$. We show that no such extension exists in characteristic 3. Together with the obstruction coming from the even part for characteristic $0$ and $p > 3$, this gives non-existence for a field $\mathbb{K}$ of characteristic different from $2$.

title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.

title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for irreversible dynamics via adaptive Dyson expansion
abstract: In this note, we study a broad class of time-dependent and irreversible dynamics for quantum spin systems in both finite and infinite volume. We develop a simple and flexible strategy for expanding commutators of the form $[A,τ_{s,t} \, B]$ in terms of self-avoiding paths of sets, where $A$ and $B$ are local operators and $τ_{s,t}$ is the Heisenberg time evolution. This adaptive Dyson expansion requires no backwards time evolution and is thus also applicable to irreversible dynamics. Furthermore, we discuss how such an expansion directly implies Lieb-Robinson bounds. A central feature of our result is that the obtained Lieb-Robinson bounds are independent of any Hamiltonian and dissipative on-site terms of the generator.

title: New bound on the Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^4$
abstract: We obtain a slight improvement to the trilinear bound of Guth-Zahl by application of Wang-Zahl's resolution of 3-D Kakeya to tubes inside a thickened neighborhood of a variety. This is combined with the planebrush argument of Katz and Zahl to obtain the new bound of 3.073.

title: A unified approach to the definition of anti-algebras
abstract: We introduce the $\mathfrak M$arseille anti-construction $\mathfrak{Ma}$ for varieties of algebras defined by multilinear identities of degree $3$, obtained by changing the sign of the right-nested part of each defining polynomial. This gives, for any variety $\Var$, a new variety $\mathfrak{Ma}$-$\Var$ that generalizes antiassociative algebras and the recently studied anti-Novikov and anti-right-symmetric $\big($pre-Jacobi--Jordan$\big)$ algebras. We describe free objects in several $\mathfrak{Ma}$-varieties. On the operadic level, over a field of characteristic $\mathrm{char}\,\Bbbk\neq 2$, we show $(\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}\Var)^{(!)}=\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}(\Var^{(!)})$ and that the Dong property is preserved by $\mathfrak{Ma}.$ Finally, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition for $\mathfrak{Ma}\text{-}\Var=\Var$. The second part of the paper is dedicated to another type of anti-algebras, called $\mathcal{M}anin$ anti-algebras. We give the description of this type of algebras via calculation of the white Manin product of suitable operads and present various examples of known $\mathcal{M}anin$ anti-algebras. In the end, we proved that the symmetric affinization of an algebra gives a Jacobi-Jordan algebra if and only if the original algebra is a $\mathcal{M}a$-Novikov algebra, that is, an analog of a well-known result about affinization of Novikov algebras given by Balinskii and Novikov.

title: Operator Algebras and Their Applications
abstract: We introduce a new class of commutative associative algebras whose structural constants are linear operators acting in a linear topological space. An analogue of the theory of monogenic functions is developed for such algebras. It is shown that the components of monogenic functions satisfy second-order operator-differential equations. This approach provides a constructive method for obtaining solutions of various partial differential and integro-differential equations. Several illustrative examples are presented.

title: $G$-Equivariant Hilbert Schemes and Quadratic Forms
abstract: For a finite abelian group $G$ acting linearly on the plane let $\mathcal{X}$ be the associated quotient stack. We analyze a fine moduli space which parameterizes zero dimensional substacks of $\mathcal{X}$ whose corresponding subschemes of the plane have a given representation type, denoted by $\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]}$. By means of a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem of Toën we give explicit representation theoretic formulas of $\dim(\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]})$ for all $ρ\in \operatorname{Rep}(G)$ which are similar to the McKay correspondence. We also give a classification of all such quotient stacks according to an associated quadratic form called the Euler form. For $[\mathbb{A}^2/μ_n]$ given by the cyclic action $ζ\cdot (x,y) = (ζx, ζ^{-1} y)$, we give an interpretation of the corresponding Euler form in terms of border strips which may be removed by a diagram, an equational characterization of $n$-core partitions, and the number of significant arrows of a monomial ideal as defined in "Smooth and Irreducible Multigraded Hilbert Schemes" by D. Maclagan and G. Smith.

title: Childcare Waitlists
abstract:
Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity.
  We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.

title: SDDP has polynomial iteration complexity in the horizon
abstract: Stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) and its variants are run in practice with forward passes that sample the noise at random. Recent iteration-complexity results favour another choice: when the trial points are selected deterministically, for instance along the scenario with the largest gap, the number of iterations is polynomial in the horizon $T$, whereas every bound we know of for randomly sampled forward passes is exponential in $T$. We show that this is not intrinsic to random sampling, for a broad class of trajectory-following dynamic programming algorithms, which includes SDDP, stochastic dual dynamic integer programming and stochastic Lipschitz dynamic programming. With random sampling, and with Lipschitz constants, diameters and per-stage loss ranges bounded independently of the stage and of the horizon, the expected number of iterations whose policy is not $T\varepsilon$-optimal is $O(T\varepsilon^{-(d+1)})$, where $d$ is the state dimension: linear in $T$, as for deterministic selection rules. The proof needs no particular scenario to be sampled: the gap between the expected cost of the current policy and the current lower bound equals the expected sum of one-step Bellman residuals along the sampled path, and Lipschitz cuts that are tight at the visited states turn the positive residuals into permanent increases of a bounded potential. The results extend to noise without finite support, to backward passes on a sample average approximation, and to stationary and periodic infinite-horizon SDDP with geometric pass lengths.

title: An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
abstract: We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.

title: Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
abstract: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.

title: Median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for nested integration
abstract: Nested integrals $\int f\left(\int g(\boldsymbol{y},\boldsymbol{x})\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{x}\right)\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{y}$ where $\boldsymbol{y}\in[0,1]^{d_1}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\in[0,1]^{d_2}$ frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate $α+3/2-ε$ for any $ε>0$ can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where $α\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.

title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta-Iovita-Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard-Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao-Liu.

title: Global obstruction property and its applications
abstract: We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite. For each Artin algebra $A$, we construct an algebra $\mathcal{G}(A)$ satisfying GOP by using triangular matrix extensions. We show that $\text{fin.dim}\mathcal{G}(A)=\text{fin.dim} A+2$ and that $A$ and $\mathcal{G}(A)$ are singularly equivalent. Finally, we give a pair of derived equivalent finite-dimensional algebras for which GOP holds on only one side.

title: Minor exclusion and planar rigidity
abstract:
We prove that every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph which is quasi-isometric to a graph excluding a countable clique as a minor is quasi-isometric to a planar graph. Consequently, every finitely generated group with such a quasi-isometry is virtually planar, meaning that some finite-index subgroup admits a planar Cayley graph.
  We also show that a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph admitting a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding some finite minor admits a regular map into a bounded-degree planar graph. If the source is accessible, the target need only exclude a countable clique. Combined with work of Mackay, Spriano, and the present author, this shows that a finitely presented group admits a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding a countable clique if and only if it is virtually planar.

title: On $m$-fullness in number fields
abstract: We prove asymptotic formulas for the number of $m$-full ideals of bounded norm in a given ideal class and for the number of $m$-full algebraic integers of bounded Weil height.

title: On the Imaginary Part of $ζ'/ζ$
abstract: We derive an explicit zero-side formula for the imaginary part of a smooth truncation of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function. The resulting kernel is the odd companion of the Fejér kernel in Montgomery's pair-correlation identity. Motivated by the recent breakthrough of Anthropic's Claude \cite{Claude26}, we also give an expository account of how the real-part identity can be turned into a matrix problem, overcoming the clustering obstruction for zeros off the critical line. Finally, we discuss how the new imaginary-part identity may contain additional information about such clustering.

title: Sharp lower bound of the first eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian under integral Ricci curvature
abstract: We prove a sharp Zhong-Yang type lower bound for the first nonzero eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian on closed manifolds with small integral Ricci curvature for $p \geq 2$. The proof combines a global elliptic estimate obtained by Sobolev truncation with strict perturbations of one-dimensional comparison profiles.

title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
abstract:
Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$.
  In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.

title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels
abstract: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.

title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
abstract: For a positive integer $d$, let $Δ_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $Δ_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.

title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
The finite basis problem for varieties generated by all semirings of a fixed order
abstract: Let $\Avar_n$ and $\VV_n$ be the varieties generated by all $n$-element additively idempotent semirings (ai-semirings) and all $n$-element semirings with commutative addition, respectively, in the signature $(+,\cdot)$ without constants. We prove that both varieties are finitely based if and only if $n\leq2$. The five-element case follows from cyclic identities and a structural analysis of products of squares. For $n\geq6$, each variety contains a finite inherently nonfinitely based ai-semiring. We also prove $\VV_n\cap\AI=\Avar_n$ for every $n$, where $\AI$ is the variety of all ai-semirings.

title: Products of Boolean Clones up to Minion Homomorphisms
abstract: We study the minion homomorphism poset of multisorted Boolean clones. Our main result completely determines the subposet induced by products of Boolean clones: every inequality between prod- ucts is induced by inequalities between their Boolean factors. Furthermore, we determine the minion cores of all products of Boolean clones, thereby identifying canonical representatives of their minion homomorphic equivalence classes.

title: Non-Existence of Abelian KS-Algebras in $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ for $n \geq 3$
abstract: We prove that $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ contains no abelian Kadison--Singer algebra for any $n \geq 3$.

title: Quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$
abstract: We compute quasi-derivations of Block Lie algebras $\mathcal{B}(q)$. In particular, we prove that $\mathcal{B}(q)$ has various nontrivial quasi-derivations, i.e., quasi-derivations different from derivations and $δ$-derivations. As corollaries, we have the complete description of $δ$-derivations, $δ$-biderivations, and transposed $δ$-Poisson structures on $\mathcal{B}(q)$. In particular, $\mathcal{B}(q),$ up to isomorphisms, admits only one nontrivial transposed $δ$-Poisson structure if $q\in \mathbb Z$ and $\mathcal{B}(q)$ does not admits nontrivial transposed $δ$-Poisson structures if $q\notin \mathbb Z.$

title: Odd order cases of Chowla's averages over arbitrary rectangles
abstract:
Let $λ$ be the Liouville function. In this paper we prove an average form of Chowla Conjecture for even $k $. that is, for every fixed even integer $k\geq 2$, we prove that \[ \lim_{\min\{M,N\}\to \infty}\frac{1}{MN}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{n=1}^Nλ(m)λ(m+a_1n)\cdotsλ(m+a_kn)=0. \]
  We construct a stationary model for both averaging variables, derive the finite conditional-entropy estimates. A comparison of overlapping intervals on the logarithmic axis then forces this function to vanish.

title: Derived plethystic algebra
abstract: We prove comparison results about $\infty$-categories of derived commutative rings with extra algebraic structure. For example, we show that several notions of derived $δ$-rings agree and obtain similar results for derived $λ$-rings, derived binomial rings, and derived Boolean rings. Our comparison results apply more generally to modules over a specific kind of monad on derived rings that we call derived plethory.

title: Connectivity, toughness, and hamiltonicity of simplicial polytopes
abstract:
For every $d\ge4$, every prescribed connectivity $r\ge d$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a simplicial $d$-polytope whose graph has connectivity exactly $r$, is nontraceable, and has toughness less than $\varepsilon$. Thus the classical theorems of Whitney (1931) and Tutte (1956), which guarantee hamiltonicity under sufficiently high connectivity in dimension three, have no higher-dimensional counterpart. This answers a question posed by Bojan Mohar in 2001 on whether sufficiently high connectivity guarantees hamiltonicity of $4$-polytopal graphs and the connectivity questions raised by Ikegami, Maezawa, and Zamfirescu in 2021.
  For fixed $d\ge4$, $r\ge d$, and integer $k\ge2$, the examples can be chosen to have no closed spanning walk with at most $k$ visits per vertex, no spanning tree with degrees at most $k$, and nontraceable prisms.
  For fixed $d$ and $r$, we obtain graphs on $n$ vertices whose longest paths and cycles contain $O(\sqrt n)$ vertices. Consequently, the family of simplicial $d$-polytopes with connectivity exactly $r$ has Grünbaum--Walther shortness coefficient zero and shortness exponent at most $1/2$.

title: Reciprocal LCM powers and Robin's criterion
abstract: For $κ> 1$, we study the reciprocal LCM-power function \[ σ^{[κ]}_{-1}(n) := \sum_{d \mid n}μ(d)\,σ_{-1}(n / d)^κ. \] We determine its average and extremal orders. A natural Robin-scale normalization is strictly increasing in $κ$ and tends to $σ_{-1}$, yielding an RH-equivalent criterion. Unconditionally, the corresponding Robin inequality holds eventually on every bounded parameter interval. Directed interval arithmetic proves the inequality for each $n > 5040$ and $1 < κ\le 100{,}000$.

title: Algebraic Vector Bundles on Cluster Varieties
abstract: We study algebraic vector bundles on cluster varieties. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, every algebraic vector bundle is trivial on a cluster variety with principal coefficients at an acyclic seed of irreducible finite Dynkin type. The proof is based on integral contractions of cellular $\mathbb A^1$-chain complexes and successive freezing. We also construct smooth cluster varieties admitting indecomposable rank-two vector bundles, whose nontriviality is detected by quadratic Euler classes. The cellular calculation also gives a criterion for stable freeness and computes integral real cohomology and the images of cycle class maps.

title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent, not necessarily identically distributed, random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\). Let \(S_n\) denote the sum, let \(Σ=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\), and let \(G\sim N(0,Σ)\). Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}Σ}{\|Σ\|}, \qquad v(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(Σ^2)}{\|Σ\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions \(r(Σ)\le C_Σv(Σ)\) and \(v(Σ)\ge6\), we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(Σ)^{3/2}}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the fixed parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The bound is uniform at the endpoint \(v(Σ)=6\), without a logarithmic loss. Its main feature is the combination of the \(n^{-1}\) rate with dependence on effective rank, including this endpoint. Consequently, the bound can vanish when \(r(Σ)=o(n^{2/3})\), even when \(p\) is much larger than \(n\). The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof builds on the Fourier and symmetrization methods of \citet{GoetzeZaitsev2014}, combined with moment matching, truncation, and comparison estimates that retain the covariance structure.

title: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
abstract: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.

title: Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wiśniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.

title: Pointed Gromov-Hausdorff Distance between $l^p$-Wedge Sums and Isometric Embeddings of $l^\infty$
abstract: The paper studies $l^p$-wedge sums of metric spaces and provides a two-sided estimate for the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff distance between them. Using an upper bound for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, the existence of an isometric embedding of $l^\infty$ into the Gromov-Hausdorff space of all non-empty metric spaces is proved.

title: Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles
abstract: Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_δ$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.

title: A higher-dimensional Schrödinger maximal estimate along families of bi-Lipschitz curves
abstract: Let $Θ\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 1$ be compact with upper Minkowski dimension $β$, and let $γ(x,t,θ)$ be a family of curves which is bi-Lipschitz in the first variable and Lipschitz in the last two. We prove the maximal estimate $$\left\|\sup_{(τ,θ)\in[0,1)\timesΘ}\left|e^{iτΔ}f(γ(\,\cdot\,,τ,θ))\right|\right\|_{L^2(B^n_1)}\lesssim_s\|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb{R}^n)},$$ for every $s>\tfrac{n(β+1)}{2(n+1)}$, in the range $0\leβ\le n-1$. In the range $n-1<β\leq n$ we prove the threshold $s>\min\big\lbrace\fracβ2 + \frac 1{2(n+1)},\frac n2\big\rbrace$. The proof relies on a fractal $L^2$ estimate of Du--Zhang. We also use the temporal localization of Lee, the locally constant property, and a counting argument allowed by the Lipschitz properties of the curve.

title: Maximal Order Type and Width of the h-Preorder on Finite Labeled Trees
abstract: We establish tight bounds for the width and maximal order type of the h-preorder on Q-labeled trees in terms of the corresponding invariants of well-quasi-order Q.

title: The Game Chromatic Number of Complete Multipartite Graphs with Singletons and Large Parts
abstract: We study the game chromatic number of complete multipartite graphs whose parts are either singletons or are of size at least four. Building on the work of PawełObszarski et al., we give a formula in terms of the ordered part sizes, and the number of singleton parts.

title: Asymptotic Root Dynamics under Repeated and Fractional Integration
abstract: Fix a polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}a_jx^j$ of degree $m$, and let $I_kP$ be its $k$-fold antiderivative with all integration constants zero. Borwein, Chen, and Dilcher proved that, after $x=ky$, the nonzero zeros of $I_kP$ converge to the zeros of $L[P](y)=\sum_j a_j j! y^j$. That fixes a direction but neither a position nor successive differences. We compute the next two terms at a simple nonzero zero $λ$ of $L[P]$; these supply both. Integer-order and Riemann-Liouville integration reduce, after scaling, to one rational family $c_j(h)=\prod_{\ell\le j}(1+\ell h)^{-1}$ sampled at $h=1/k$ and $h=1/α$; the scaled zero is analytic in $h$ at $h=0$. We prove $r_k=kλ+C_P(λ)+D_P(λ)/k+O(k^{-2})$ with explicit $C_P$ and $D_P$, whence $r_k-r_{k-1}=λ-D_P(λ)/(k(k-1))+O(k^{-3})$ and $r'(α)=λ-D_P(λ)/α^{2}+O(α^{-3})$. So $λ$ is at once the scaled root location, the limiting discrete spacing, and the limiting continuous-order velocity, and $C_P(λ)$ is the offset of an asymptotic line. For binomials the limiting spacing is a multiple of a gamma-ratio quantity (the Factorial Fraction), and the nonzero reduced roots form an exact regular polygon at every positive order. For real quadratics the collision order of two branches is explicit and, under nondegeneracy hypotheses, positive exactly when $P$ has distinct real zeros and $L[P]$ has none; in arbitrary degree the collision discriminant carries a universal factor supported at negative orders, leaving a factor of degree at most $m(m-1)/2$. All trajectories form one plane curve of degree $m$ with leading form $L[P]$, whose collisions are discriminant values of the order projection and whose order-zero end is governed by a harmonic transform dual to the arithmetic one at infinity. The case $λ=0$ is rigid: the origin is pinned at every positive order.

title: Complex slices, inverses, and deformations of a three-dimensional real algebra
