abstract: We study the real three-dimensional unital algebra with basis $\{1,i,j\}$ and products $i^2=j^2=-1,\quad ij=0,\quad ji=i+j$. Its quadratic and power-associative elements form the union of exactly three complex subalgebras; their nonzero elements are precisely those with a two-sided inverse, which is unique. Every nonzero subalgebra contains the unit, and every element outside these three planes generates the whole algebra. We classify one-sided inverses, including the singular cases, and show that two-sided invertibility does not imply cancellation. The multiplication algebra is $M_3(\mathbb{R})$, so the algebra is absolutely central simple. Its derivations vanish, its automorphism group is trivial, and its commutator Lie algebra is $\mathbb{R}\oplus\mathfrak{aff}(1)$. Its unique antiautomorphism is involutive, and its complexification admits no complex-linear structurable involution. Finally, replacing $ji=i+j$ by $ji=t(i+j)$ gives real algebras $\mathcal{A}_t$ with $\mathcal{A}_s\cong\mathcal{A}_t$ exactly when $s^2=t^2$. We describe the exceptional parameters and thereby exhibit nontrivial deformations of the original algebra.

title: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
abstract:
Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$.
  The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a quasi-compact perfectoid source can still have an orbit closure with nonempty interior. For every finite extension $F/\mathbb Q_p$ and $d\geq3$, we construct a closed smooth irreducible non-quasi-compact curve in $Ω_F^{d-1}$ with dense orbit under a fixed diagonal one-parameter subgroup. We also construct a $\mathbb Q_p$-defined analytic map from the open unit disc to $\mathbf P^2$ with dense $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit, and an analytic map from a one-dimensional affinoid perfectoid torus to $\mathbf P^2$ whose $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit closure has nonempty interior.

title: High-Index Asymptotics of Mathieu Spectral Gaps and Splittings
abstract: Consider the Mathieu operator $L=-d^2/dx^2+2a\cos(2x)$ for fixed $a\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$. For large enough $n$, the periodic ($n$ even) or anti-periodic ($n$ odd) problem on $[0,π]$ has exactly two algebraically simple eigenvalues $λ_n^-,λ_n^+$ in the disc $|λ-n^2|<1$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $λ_n^+-λ_n^-=\pm\frac{8(a/4)^n}{[(n-1)!]^2}\exp\left[-\frac{a^2(n+2)}{4(n^2-1)^2}-\frac{15a^4}{128n^7}+O(n^{-8})\right]$, where the sign depends on the labelling. For real $a$ with $λ_n^-<λ_n^+$, this difference is the length of the $n$th spectral gap. Expanding the exponential determines the relative corrections of orders $n^{-4}$ to $n^{-7}$, beyond the correction $-a^2/(4n^3)$ obtained by Anahtarci and Djakov (2012) with a relative $O(n^{-4})$ remainder. By isospectrality, the same formula holds for the potential $ce^{-2ix}+de^{2ix}$ with $a^2=cd\ne0$.

title: Minimax Rates for Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals
abstract: We study the two-sample estimation of the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional under projected $r$-th moment assumptions. Let $N=n\wedge m$, where $n$ and $m$ are two sample sizes. We establish the minimax rates in the noncritical regimes. When $p<r<2p$, the minimax risk is of order $N^{-(r-p)/r}$, while for $r>2p$ it is of order $N^{-1/2}$. In both cases, the natural plug-in estimator is minimax rate-optimal. At the endpoint $r=p$, the minimax risk is bounded away from zero, so uniformly consistent estimation is impossible. At the critical order $r=2p$, we obtain the exact worst-case rate of the plug-in estimator and a lower bound for the minimax risk, leaving a logarithmic gap between the lower and upper bounds. The exact minimax rate in this critical case remains open.

title: Equivariant Steklov homogenisation and stability of spectral representations
abstract: We prove that isolated spectral clusters preserve their finite-group representation under equivariant spectral convergence. In particular, an irreducible limiting eigenspace cannot split into several nearby eigenvalues, while an isotypic limiting eigenspace imposes corresponding divisibility constraints on the multiplicities in the approximating cluster. We then construct a one-parameter equivariant Steklov homogenisation on closed orientable surfaces, allowing Laplace spectral representations to be transferred to Steklov spectral clusters. Applied to the hyperbolic surfaces of Fortier Bourque, Gruda-Mediavilla, Petri, and Pineault, this yields first Steklov multiplicities 16 and 21 in genera 10 and 17, and at least 24 in genus 37. These examples give counterexamples to Jammes's conjecture on first Steklov multiplicity.

title: Pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise Hölder continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise Hölder continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.

title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
abstract: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.

title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincaré series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gröbner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.

title: Frugal coloring in planar graphs with maximum degree 4 and 5
abstract: A proper coloring of vertices of a graph $G$ is called $t$-frugal if no color appears more than $t$ times in the neighborhood of any vertex of $G$. While $1$-frugal coloring coincides with $2$-distance coloring, we study $2$-frugal colorings of planar graphs with maximum degree $4$ and $5$, respectively. We prove that every planar graph with maximum degree $4$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $7$ colors, while a planar graph with maximum degree $5$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $10$ colors. The results present variations of parts of the famous Wegner's conjecture, which for planar graphs with maximum degree $Δ\in\{4,\ldots,7\}$ states that their $2$-distance chromatic number is at most $Δ+5$.

title: The first homology of square-section braid groups
abstract: We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.

title: Ultrafilter characters and local $π$-bases
abstract: We completely resolve Question~5.3 of Kania's paper \cite{Kania} and establish a more general realization theorem. We show that for infinite cardinals $μ\leqslantν<κ<λ$, a space with \[ \pc(X)=μ,\qquad\pcl(X)=ν,\qquad \pcc(X)=κ,\qquad\pcd(X)=λ\] exists if and only if $κ\leqslant2^μ$. The witnesses may be zero-dimensional and Tychonoff spaces, of the least possible cardinality $λ$. They may have the least possible number of non-isolated points, or alternatively be crowded. The main ingredient is an exact computation of the centered local $π$-character of star filter spaces in terms of ultrafilter character, obtained from a finite selection lemma for filter pushforwards. We also construct a single space with countable $r$-linked local $π$-bases for every finite $r$, centered value $ω_1$, and any prescribed decreasing value greater than $ω_1$.

title: Triality rotation of connections and Dirac operators on SU(3)
abstract:
We show how triality, the symmetry permuting the three 8-dimensional representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$, can also appear as a symmetry of geometric objects such as connections and Dirac operators. Take any Riemannian metric $g$ on the manifold $M = \mathrm{SU}(3)$ and let $
abla$ be a metric connection on $TM$. Using an explicit model of Clifford multiplication by deformed Okubo products, we combine spinorial lifts with isometries $TM \simeq S^+ \simeq S^-$ to show that $
abla$ can be rotated into two new metric connections on $TM$. So there is a canonical $\mathbb{Z}_3$-orbit of metric connections determined by $(g, 
abla)$, with no other choices. The three connections coincide when $g$ is bi-invariant and $
abla$ belongs to the Cartan-Schouten line, but in general they are different. The rotations of $
abla$ preserve the norm of the curvature, so they define a new $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetry of the moduli space of Yang-Mills connections on $TM$. They also preserve the Chern-Simons 3-form and adjoint Yang-Mills-Higgs functionals. After choosing an orientation on $M$, the rotated connections define three self-adjoint, Dirac-type operators on the spinor bundle. We prove that these operators are natural, in the sense that they commute with the Kosmann derivatives of spinors along all invariant Killing vector fields that preserve $
abla$. We also show that they are not isospectral, in general. This is verified by computing the simplest eigenvalue for the Levi-Civita connection and observing that it splits among the three operators as the bi-invariant metric on $M$ is deformed to one with isometry group $(\mathrm{SU}(3) 	imes \mathrm{SU}(2) 	imes \mathrm{U}(1)) / \mathbb{Z}_6$. Finally, we outline how the constructions in the paper may extend to general 8-manifolds with a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)$-structure.

title: Normal bundles of hyperelliptic curves and uniform propagation of semistability
abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus $g\ge2$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We prove that the normal bundle of the embedding of $C$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$, $n\ge3$, by the complete linear series of a general line bundle of degree $n+g$ is semistable if and only if $n\ge3g+1$. By openness, general complete embeddings of general curves of genus $g$ also have semistable normal bundle when $n\ge3g+1$. We then show that a general nonspecial curve of genus two and degree $d$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ has semistable normal bundle except when $(n,d)$ is $(3,5)$, $(4,6)$, $(5,7)$ or $(6,8)$. The degenerations used in genus two extend to every genus $g\ge3$: semistability in all nonspecial degrees and dimensions follows from the cases $0\le d-n-g\le4g-4$. Together with a separate estimate for large $n$, this reduces semistability in each fixed genus to finitely many cases. The proofs combine degenerations to reducible nodal curves, explicit bounds on the degrees of subsheaves, and, in genus two, finitely many exact computations, which are provided as ancillary files.

title: Precise propagation rates of the fractional Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries
abstract:
In this paper, we determine the propagation rates of the Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries and fractional diffusion $(-Δ)^s$ $(0<s<1)$, which was considered in \cite{CDN26} as a model for species spreading, where the density function $u(t,x)$ satisfies the fractional Fisher-KPP equation $u_t+(-Δ)^su=f(u)$ over a one-dimensional spatial domain $(g(t), h(t))$, representing the expanding population range, with $x=g(t)$ and $x=h(t)$ the free boundaries. It was shown in \cite{CDN26} that the model is well-posed, and its long-time dynamics exhibits a spreading-vanishing dichotomy. We show in this paper that, when spreading occurs,
  \[ \begin{cases} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\left(\frac{2^{1-2s}μ}{1-2s}\right)^{1/(2s)} & \mbox{ if $s\in(0,1/2)$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t\ln t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t\ln t} =μ& \mbox{ if $s=1/2$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t} =c_0(s) & \mbox{ if $s\in(1/2,1)$}, \end{cases} \] where $c_0(s)\in (0,\infty)$ is uniquely determined by the associated semi-wave problem. The level sets of $u(t,x)$ propagate with the same rates as the free boundaries. The proof uses delicate upper and lower solutions constructed from a smooth profile function in the case $s\in (0, 1/2]$, and from the semi-wave profile when $s\in (1/2, 1)$.

title: A conditional bound $Λ\le0.13963$ for the de Bruijn--Newman constant
abstract: Assuming that $ζ(s)$ has no nontrivial zero with $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 7/8$, as asserted in a recent unrefereed preprint of OpenAI, we obtain $Λ\le 13963/100000 = 0.13963$ for the de Bruijn-Newman constant. A published Polymath boundary computation supplies a finite-region strip of half-width $1/5$. We derive an approximation on $3 \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 6$ from its general Riemann-Siegel coefficient bounds. At height $61/20$, a fixed cutoff permits two differentiations, and comparison with $ζ$ bounds both the zero-density kernel and its vertical derivative. A new conjugate-pair inequality and a twenty-four-step strip comparison give the stated bound. The finite scalar and polynomial certificates are included in the paper; earlier comparisons giving $0.17973$, $0.17172$, and $0.16408$ are retained to show the source of the gain. The argument uses neither Gordon's analytic inputs nor Gomila's new computations. The seven-eighths hypothesis remains an assumption, and the published numerical boundary input is retained.

title: On the Isotropy Groups of Locally Finite Derivations of Laurent Polynomial Algebras
abstract: Let $A_n=\mathbb{k}[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm1}]$ be a Laurent polynomial algebra over a field $\mathbb{k}$ of characteristic zero. We determine explicitly the automorphisms commuting with each locally finite derivation \[ D_μ=\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i x_i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}, \qquad μ=(μ_1,\ldots,μ_n)^T\in\Bbbk^n. \] These are precisely the automorphisms $ρ(x_i)=λ_i x^{m_i}$, where $λ_i\in\mathbb{k}^\ast$, the exponent vectors $m_i$ are the columns of a matrix $M_ρ\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)$, and $μ^TM_ρ=μ^T$. We also give an explicit parametrization in dimension two and relate these automorphisms to symmetries of diagonal flows on algebraic tori.

title: Efficient lifts into odd dimensions of Spherical $5$- and $7$-designs with Balanced Halves
abstract: We propose constructions of spherical $5$- and $7$-designs in odd dimensions by lifting balanced halves of even-dimensional designs to several layers of suitable latitudes. For every odd dimension, we obtain an explicit spherical $5$-design with at most $60(d^2-1)$ points, attaining the optimal quadratic order in the dimension. Assuming Zauner's conjecture, this bound improves to $7.5(d-1)^2$. For every odd $d \geq 9$, we also construct a spherical $7$-design with $110M$ points from a complex projective $3$-design with $M$ points in $\mathbb{CP}^{(d-3)/2}$.

title: Generic mean curvature flow has finitely many singularities
abstract: We show that for a generic compact initial surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and any generic compact initial mean convex hypersurface in higher dimensions, the mean curvature flow encounters only finitely many singularities. This resolves the full generic Morse regularity conjectures of Ilmanen and Colding-Minicozzi-Pedersen in the above two cases. More generally, we show that if a mean curvature flow of a compact hypersurface has only multiplicity one spherical and cylindrical singularities, then after a small perturbation of the initial condition only non-degenerate cylindrical and spherical singularities appear.

title: Numerical Stability of Extended-Domain Spectral Collocation: Floating-Point Regularization and an Equilibrium Law for the Frame Constants
abstract: Extended-domain spectral collocation expands the solution of a boundary value problem in the Laplacian eigenbasis of an enclosing box and collocates at as many nodes as modes. The square system is exponentially ill-conditioned, and the impossibility theorem for equispaced data rules out stable geometric convergence; yet such solvers converge geometrically to a few orders of magnitude above the unit roundoff. We explain why in one dimension. The collocation solution is the solution operator applied to the interpolant of the data in an operator-dependent test space whose Lebesgue constant must grow exponentially for geometric convergence, so exact solutions can amplify data errors exponentially. In floating-point arithmetic the error of any coefficient vector is bounded by its nodal residual, its distance to a competitor and two frame constants, a leakage and a restricted Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund constant, bounded uniformly in the number of modes at a fixed positive threshold; for a backward-stable solve, under a condition on the perturbed matrix, the bound is uniform in the conditioning for suitably analytic data and, with computed constants, within a factor of about ten of the error floor of a direct solver. For the Poisson operator the rate of the two constants along the tail of the spectrum is given by a constrained equilibrium problem of logarithmic potential theory. For an interval of length $L$ extended by $δ$ at each end, the problems for $δ$ and $L^2/(4δ)$ are dual, the rate is linear for $δ= L/2$, and it starts with slope minus the fraction of the extended domain occupied by the extension, so for $δ< L/2$ the leakage constant obeys no power law with the exponent of the end of the spectrum. In experiments, convection--diffusion operators behave like the Poisson operator at moderate Péclet numbers.

title: Minimizing tangent maps into complex projective space
abstract: We classify all nonconstant smooth harmonic maps $\mathbb{S}^2\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ whose 0-homogeneous extensions are minimizing: they are, respectively, isometric embeddings or holomorphic isometric embeddings composed with a Hopf map.

title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics
abstract: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.

title: Representing the Non-dominated Set of Multi-objective Optimization Problems with Polyhedral Ordering Cones
abstract: In the literature, research on representing the non-dominated set has focused almost exclusively on multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-dominance. However, general ordering cones are used to incorporate preferences of decision makers into the optimization process and to model other specific types of optimization problems, such as ordinal optimization problems. In this work, we consider several representation approaches based on representation relations in the context of multi-objective optimization problems with polyhedral ordering cones. Our main research question is whether existing theory and solution approaches developed for the Pareto case can be used to address the more general setting.

title: Remarks on temperature-dependent Cahn--Hilliard equations
abstract: We recall several derivations of temperature-dependent Cahn-Hilliard equations. The resulting equations are systems of mixed order. For a suitable subclass of equations we discuss its local-in-time well-posedness based on $L^p$-maximal regularity theory. We also discuss stability of equilibria.

title: Classes of Subgroups of a finite group with isomorphic quotient groups
abstract: In this paper, we study the poset QIso(G) of classes of subgroups of finite group G having isomorphic quotients. Particularly, we study it for finite abelian groups and for some classes of non-abelian metacyclic groups namely, dihedral groups Dn, the group U2np and affine groups Aff(F) over finite field F. In the case of abelian groups G, we show that QIso(G) and Iso(G) are isomorphic. We show that cyclic groups are the only groups for which QIso(G) is isomorphic to its subgroup lattice. We also show that cyclic groups are the only nilpotent groups for which QIso(G) and its lattice of normal subgroups are isomorphic. We characterize finite 2-groups all of whose subgroups are q-self dual with QIso(G) being a chain. We also characterize all p-groups G of order at most p4 whose QIso(G) is a chain.

title: On the number of conjugacy classes of finite solvable groups of order divisible by $p^2$
abstract: In 2003, Héthelyi and Külshammer proved that if $G$ is a finite solvable group and $p$ is a prime such that $p^2$ divides $|G|$, then $k(G)\geq (49p+1)/60$, and they constructed an infinite family of groups for which this bound was claimed to be attained. We point out that the groups in this family are not Frobenius groups, so that their class numbers are considerably larger than stated, and that in fact the bound is never attained. We then determine the best possible bound of this shape: we show that $k(G)\geq (49p+7)/60$ for all primes $p$, which is sharp for $p=17$, and that $k(G)\geq (49p+451)/60$ for all primes $p>2719$, which is sharp for infinitely many primes $p$. Thus the slope $49/60$ found by Héthelyi and Külshammer is best possible, but the correct additive constant is $451/60$ rather than $1/60$.

title: On the composition of permutons
abstract:
Permutons can be thought of as "continuum limits" of permutations of diverging size, which encode information about the number of occurrences of any given finite subpattern. We construct a natural composition operation on permutons, analogous to composition of permutations, and explore its properties via a correspondence between permutons, Markov kernels, and Markov operators.
  We show that no extension of permutation composition to permutons can be (jointly) continuous with respect to the usual "weak" topology on permutons, but we construct a "strong" topology with respect to which composition is jointly continuous. Moreover, we characterize strong convergence of sequences of permutations of diverging size: a sequence of permutations converges strongly if and only if it converges weakly and its limit is the transpose of the graph of a measure-preserving function. The key insight behind these results is to apply functional analysis to certain operators associated to permutons; with this shift in perspective, our results have elegant and relatively "soft" proofs.
  As an application, we describe the permuton limit of a product of finitely many independent uniformly sampled separable permutations and give a formula for the expectation of this limit. We also show that in this case, as the number of compositions goes to infinity, the aforementioned expectation tends to the uniform permuton.

title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
abstract: Practical ship design requires localized refinement and performance evaluation. This paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized hull optimization. Parametric masking during dataset generation restricts geometric changes to selected variables, including the bulbous bow and forebody, while preserving full-hull continuity. Surrogate-assisted sequential Monte Carlo sampling targets reduced predicted calm-water resistance, with stability retained through training data and displacement matched during screening. An automated viscous free-surface CFD pipeline, validated against measurements for two benchmark container ships, evaluates a generated variant and GenHull E, a hull refined by a naval architect within the same representation. At matched KRISO Container Ship (KCS) displacement, the generated variant has comparable total resistance at $F_n=0.195$ but 45-50% higher resistance at $F_n=0.250$ and $0.260$, missed by empirical screening. GenHull E achieves 6-8% lower total resistance up to $F_n=0.240$ but higher resistance above $F_n=0.250$ as opposing friction and pressure trends reverse the gains. Aggregating resistance across this crossover can conceal tradeoffs that emerge when friction and pressure components are evaluated separately. The assessment reveals an inability to represent a faired bulbous bow and a reward lacking viscous pressure and stability terms. These findings show how high-fidelity assessment informs improved representations and objectives for physically realizable generative designs.

title: A Vector-Valued Extension of a Theorem of Marciszewski
abstract: We establish a vector-valued extension of a theorem of Marciszewski. Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $Γ$ be a set, and let $X$ be a nonzero Banach space containing no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. We prove that if $C(K)$ embeds isomorphically into $c_0(Γ,X)$, then $C(K)$ is isomorphic to $c_0(Λ)$ for some set $Λ$. Moreover, when $Γ$ is infinite, the optimal distortion of embeddings of $C(K)$ into $c_0(Γ,X)$ equals that of embeddings into $c_0(Γ)$. The classification result answers a question posed in an earlier paper.

title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part~1: expectation under the uniform null
abstract: We study the expectation of the discrete total variation statistic $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$ of counts $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $n$ ordered bins with sample size $N$, under the uniform multinomial null. In the notation used throughout the series, a reference distribution $\mathbf r$ defines $d_{\mathbf r}(x)=\|x-N\mathbf r\|_V$; here $\mathbf r=\mathbf u$ is uniform and we write simply $d$. We obtain an exact single-sum formula, a closed form in central trinomial coefficients valid for every $n\ge2$, with one-term evaluations at $n=2,4$ and a complete D-finite characterization for $n=3$. The per-edge expectation $W_N=E|X_2-X_1|$ satisfies an exact three-term recurrence, from which we derive its complete $1/N$ expansion with the $n$-independent constant $E(d^\circ/\sqrt{Nn})\to 2/\sqrtπ$ for the cyclic statistic $d^\circ=d^\circ_{\mathbf u}$, independent of the number of bins; the complementary sparse regime (fixed $N$, $n\to\infty$) is treated in a separate paper. Conditioning on a two-bin total reduces each edge to a symmetric random walk; as the subsequent parts of the series will show, this method carries the analysis to non-uniform reference laws.

title: Critical Point Theory for the Distance Function on PL-Spaces
abstract: We study the (typical) singularities of the distance function from a point in the ambient space to a polytopal complex in Euclidean space. By means of the Goresky-MacPherson splitting we generalize the existing linear theory to the quadratic distance function. Critical points occur on `selected' strata of the PL-space, where normal Morse Data determine the change of topology. On the homology level there exist indices with multiplicities, combined in a Morse vector. We focus mainly on PL-manifolds. We give bounds, depending on the dimension of the strata. In low dimensions we describe singularity types. At the end we discuss relations with Discrete Morse Theory.

title: Towards linear growth for biprojective hypersurfaces of small dimension
abstract: After removing suitable thin subsets, we count rational points of bounded height on some hypersurfaces of small bidegree in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^3$ and in $\mathbb{P}^3\times\mathbb{P}^2$. One of the ingredients is a new estimate for the number of rational points of bounded height on diagonal quadratic surfaces which improves as the coefficients grow.

title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface
abstract: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.

title: A note on purely infinite extensions
abstract: We study a strong pure infiniteness property for extensions, and give a classification result for extensions which contains many (and possibly all) previous cases, under standard and mild assumptions. We also prove a Voiculescu-type theorem decomposition theorem for certain C*-subalgebras of a corona algebra, for which the inclusion map has this strong pure infiniteness property.

title: Hecke Eigenform Product Identities for Full-Level Hilbert Modular Forms
abstract: We study full-level Hilbert Hecke eigenform product identities over totally real fields of degree at least two, allowing arbitrary compatible narrow class characters. Combining our results with previous work, we classify products of two Eisenstein eigenforms of positive parallel integral weights and products of an Eisenstein eigenform of weight at least two with a cuspidal eigenform of positive parallel integral weight. The unique identity in each of these two classes is given by $E_{4}=60 E_{2}^{2}$ and $h_{8}=120 E_{2} \cdot h_{6}$, respectively, both over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$. The proofs use constant-term comparisons, indecomposable Fourier exponents, integrality of reciprocal Eisenstein constant terms, and a Rankin-Selberg formula for Petersson inner products. In the remaining case of a weight-one Eisenstein factor and a cuspidal factor, we also establish $h_5=12E_1(1,\varepsilon)\cdot h_4$ over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt3)$, where $\varepsilon$ is the nontrivial narrow class character. All eigenforms in these identities have unit-ideal coefficient one.

title: On Quadric Surfaces Weighted by Arbitrary Coefficients
abstract: For a non-singular quadratic form $F$ in four variables, we study integer solutions to $F=0$ with an arbitrary weight attached to one of the variables. This allows us to investigate genuinely sparse subsets of the corresponding variety. Our main input is to obtain cancellation in sums of character sums over the moduli arising in the application of the DFI's delta method to the quadratic hypersurface. This cancellation relies crucially on the equidistribution of quadratic roots and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums.

title: On Eigenvector Statistics of Large-Dimensional Sample Covariance Matrices with Applications
abstract:
We study the eigenvector-weighted spectral statistics \[
  T_n(\varphi,g)=p^{-1}tr\{\varphi(\boldsymbol{S}_n)g(\boldsymbolΣ)\} \] of large-dimensional sample covariance matrices \(\boldsymbol{S}_n\) with population covariance \(\boldsymbolΣ\). These statistics combine functions of sample eigenvalues with sample--population eigenvector overlaps and arise in statistical losses that depend on both. As the dimension and sample size grow proportionally, we establish a joint central limit theorem for \(\{T_n(\varphi_a,g_a)\}_{a=1}^r\) with multiple analytic test functions and population weights, centered by finite-dimensional deterministic equivalents. A key intermediate step is a joint Gaussian process limit for the weighted resolvent traces \[
  m_n^g(z)=p^{-1}tr\{(\boldsymbol{S}_n-z\boldsymbol{I}_p)^{-1}g(\boldsymbolΣ)\}. \] The limiting means and cross-covariances are expressed in terms of the population spectral distribution. We apply these results in two settings: one concerns the variance component of minimum-norm prediction risk, and the other concerns the Frobenius loss of fixed rotationally invariant covariance estimators. For fixed affine shrinkage rules, the loss means, variances, and cross-covariances have explicit formulas in terms of population spectral moments.

title: Robust Halo Orbit Stationkeeping Under Missed Thrust Events and Maneuver Execution Errors
abstract: Spacecraft stationkeeping is subject to various operational uncertainties such as missed thrust events, maneuver execution errors, and dynamics modeling errors. Missed thrust events are the most disruptive of these, and current practices mitigate that risk through Monte Carlo-driven heuristics and conservative margins that offer no formal safety guarantees and do not scale to multiple missed thrust events. This paper models these unplanned thruster outages through the Markov Jump System framework, and represents maneuver execution errors and dynamics linearization errors as bounded multiplicative noise. The resulting closed-loop system is a linear time-varying periodic Markov jump system with multiplicative noise, for which Lyapunov-like mean square stability and periodic set invariance conditions are derived. A linear matrix inequality-based optimal controller synthesis framework then designs a periodic, mode-dependent mean-square stable feedback policy that respects path constraints with probability one. The framework is demonstrated on the Earth-Moon 9:2 near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO), under both impulsive and low-thrust propulsion, and on a Saturn-Enceladus $L_1$ NRHO using impulsive propulsion. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations show that the spacecraft recovers from an arbitrary number of missed thrust events while respecting path constraints, and that the multiplicative noise model introduces additional robustness to maneuver execution error and linearization error.

title: On the simultaneous zero inclusion property and characterization of Inner product space
abstract: We show that if a Banach space $X$ is smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund and if satisfies the following \[0\in W(T) \implies 0\in W(T^{-1})\] for all invertible bounded linear map on $X$ then Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $X$ is symmetric. This result, therefore, characterizes the inner product spaces out of all smooth and almost locally uniformly rotund spaces having three or more dimension via simultaneous zero inclusion property, introduced by Bračič et al. [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 449 (2017) 1413-1423]. Further, this gives answers to some open questions asked by E. Poon [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 534(2024), 128052].

title: Banach space, Birkhoff--James orthogonality, James constant, von Neumann--Jordan constant
abstract:
We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Martín, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45].
  Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.

title: Gamma conjecture II and explicit Stokes data for a quadric projective bundle
abstract: We study the connection problem for the quantum differential equation of the Fano fourfold $X=\PP_{Q^3}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$. The problem is to identify its canonical asymptotic solutions with exceptional objects and compute the associated Stokes data. We use exact Mellin--Bessel integral representations and uniform vector asymptotics on sectors wider than $π$, followed by analytic continuation that preserves the Gamma framing. Cohomological chiral symmetry and mutations of exceptional collections put all eight sections at a common phase. This proves Gamma conjecture II for $X$ and determines a full exceptional collection and its Stokes and central connection matrices at the unit Novikov point and a specified admissible phase. The chiral symmetry also gives a flat symmetric bilinear pairing, an orthogonality identity for the Stokes matrix, and an integral unipotent square root of the monodromy matrix for a full turn. We obtain explicit formulas for the connection data at the opposite phase; on the Gamma lattice, the half-turn acts by tensoring with a square root of the anticanonical bundle. The same spinor integral transform constructs two canonical Gamma sections for $\PP_{Q^{2m+1}}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$, $m\geq1$, at positive parameters with distinct spectrum. Their sectors have opening greater than $π$, and their leading constants are independent of the dimension.

title: Artin-Schreier curves of prescribed p-rank without extra automorphisms
abstract: Let p be an odd prime. We study the Artin-Schreier analogue of Poonen's problem of constructing curves without extra automorphisms. An Artin-Schreier curve carries an unavoidable deck group Cp, so the smallest possible full geometric automorphism group inside the Artin-Schreier locus is Cp. We determine the exact numerical range in which this minimum is attained, for every p-rank. More precisely, for integers r >= 0 and N >= 1, there exists an Artin-Schreier curve X/Fp with g(X) = (p - 1)N/2, gamma(X) = r(p - 1), Aut_Fp(X) is isomorphic to Cp if and only if either r = 0, p does not divide N + 1, N >= 3 and (p,N) not equal to (3, 3), or r >= 1, N >= 2r and (r,N) not equal to (1, 2). All models are defined over the prime field by explicit equations together with elementary choices of auxiliary polynomials, and every excluded admissible case is shown to carry an extra geometric automorphism. The main structural input is the theorem of Valentini and Madan on the uniqueness of the rational subfield of index p outside three exceptional families. We exclude these families by intrinsic arguments: the genus and p-rank in most cases, Nakajima's bound on p-subgroups of automorphism groups of ordinary curves for the ordinary family, and the Lehr-Matignon normal form for isomorphisms of one-point covers for the monomial family.

title: Projective Differential Moment Invariants from the Viewpoint of Classical Invariant Theory
abstract:
Polynomial first-order projective differential moment invariants are investigated. The main result establishes an exact correspondence between such moment invariants and symmetric polynomial multipoint relative projective differential invariants of weight $-1$. This correspondence describes each homogeneous component with respect to moment degree and allows previously obtained results on relative projective invariants to be used for systematic construction. It is also proved that passing from the formal algebra of moments to their integral definitions introduces no additional algebraic relations among the constructed invariants.
  For low moment degrees, the absence of nontrivial invariants of degrees $1$ and $2$ is established, and a complete description of degree $3$ invariants is obtained. The ten cubic differential moments are naturally identified with the coefficients of a ternary cubic, connecting the construction with classical invariant theory. In particular, the Aronhold invariants $S$ and $T$ yield projective differential moment invariants of degrees $4$ and $6$. One of the known moment invariants of Wang et al. is shown to be proportional to $S$.
  The algebra of polynomial moment invariants is proved not to be finitely generated. The field of rational moment invariants coincides with the field of fractions of the polynomial invariant algebra. For the explicit constructions, compact multipoint representations define the corresponding moment polynomials without requiring their full expansions. These representations provide a basis for algorithmic construction and software computation of the invariants.

title: Open WDVV equations for non-commutative families of bounding cochains
abstract:
We derive the noncommutative open WDVV equations for the open Gromov-Witten superpotential introduced in joint work of the author and Solomon, extending the Solomon-Tukachinsky equations to noncommutative differential graded algebras. The resulting recursive formulas facilitate the computation of open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints for even-dimensional Lagrangians. We apply the open WDVV equations to compute all open Gromov-Witten invariants for the real loci of even-dimensional complex quadrics of dimension greater than two. These computations show that open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints can be nontrivial in arbitrary dimensions.
  We also construct a character for a natural subalgebra of big quantum cohomology associated to a Lagrangian endowed with a point-like bounding cochain. The character is in the spirit of the Kodaira-Spencer map of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono. Applying the character construction to the even-dimensional quadric illustrates how point-like bounding cochains refine the information about closed quantum cohomology obtained from weak bounding cochains of Floer theory. Open Gromov-Witten invariants with three boundary point constraints determine the two extensions of the character from the subalgebra to big quantum cohomology.

title: On the inequality $μ_3 < λ_1$ for the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator
abstract: In 1952, Pólya proved the inequality $μ_2 < λ_1$ for the eigenvalues of Dirichlet and Neumann problems in domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d \ge 2$. We show that $μ_3 < λ_1$ if $d\ge 3$. In the two-dimensional case, in 2025, Rohleder proved that $μ_3 < λ_1$ for simply connected domains. We prove that this inequality holds also true for double connected domains symmetric with respect to the origin.

title: Hausdorff Dimension and Flexibility for Attractors of Non-Uniformly Hyperbolic Flows
abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of attracting sets of three-dimensional flows whose one-dimensional quotient dynamics is non-uniformly expanding. Our main assumption is that the quotient map admits a full-branch uniformly expanding Gibbs--Markov induced map. We first prove that every such attractor contains a hyperbolic horseshoe of Hausdorff dimension strictly larger than two. As a consequence, after an arbitrarily small $C^2$ perturbation, the associated dynamical Lagrange and Markov spectra have robustly non-empty interior for an open and dense set of $C^1$-observables. We then establish intermediate dimension properties. Every admissible intermediate Hausdorff dimension is realized by an ergodic invariant measure supported on the attractor. Moreover, every intermediate stable and unstable dimension is realized by a strictly ergodic hyperbolic subsystem. The approach extends the dimension theory previously developed for geometric Lorenz attractors to more general non-uniformly hyperbolic attractors including singular-hyperbolic attractors, Rovella attractors, and broad classes of skew-product suspension flows modeled by intermittent and Benedicks--Carleson maps.

title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in Bénard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+α}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.

title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
abstract: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.

title: Strict Dirichlet Pólya Inequality for Simply Connected Planar Domains
abstract: We establish the strict Dirichlet Pólya inequality on every bounded simply connected planar domain. The proof uses a unitary boundary transport formulation of the Helmholtz equation and relates Dirichlet resonances to unitary eigenphase crossings through the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. An exact area identity yields the sharp Weyl coefficient, while a Ky Fan estimate leaves a strictly positive remainder in the counting estimate. The general case follows by conformal exhaustion.

title: Sharp power-weight estimates for the fractional spherical maximal operator
abstract:
For $0\leqα<n$, let $A_{*}^α$ denote the fractional spherical maximal operator. In this paper we characterise the range of $β$ for which the $L^p-L^q$ power-weight estimate
  \[\left\|A_{*}^α f\right\|_{L^q(|x|^{qβ})} \leq C \left\|f\right\|_{L^p(|x|^{pβ})}\] holds. In the diagonal case $p=q$, our work gives an affirmative answer to a conjecture of Lee. We prove analogous results for the lacunary fractional spherical maximal operator.

title: The strength of the minimum principle in constructive reverse mathematics
abstract: The minimum principle states that every real-valued uniformly continuous function f : X -> R on a compact metric space X attains its minimum. Working in the base system EL0 of constructive reverse mathematics, we show that the minimum principle is equivalent to weak Konig's lemma and to the Cantor intersection theorem (i.e., the contrapositive of the Heine-Borel theorem). Moreover, the above equivalence naturally extends to the equivalence between the corresponding principles with unique existence assumptions, which are then shown to be equivalent to the Fan theorem for detachable bars and the positivity property for a real-valued uniformly continuous function on a compact space. These results sharpen the equivalence among these principles obtained by Ishihara [Math. Log. Q. (1990), 237-240] and Berger and Ishihara [Math. Log. Q. (2005), 360-364] in Bishop's constructive mathematics.

title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
abstract: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.

title: Direct proofs for spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor
abstract: We give direct proofs of rigidity results for gradient Ricci solitons, compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, and critical spaces with cyclic parallel Ricci tensor. For solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds, successive traces of first-order pointwise identities yield quadratic equations for the Ricci tensor and its modification. These equations imply radial flatness and radial $Q$-flatness, respectively, and the corresponding global rigidity theorems apply. For critical spaces, comparison of two expressions for the Laplacian of the Hessian gives a pointwise tensor identity whose scalar contraction yields a weighted divergence formula. Integration then gives the vacuum static, CPE, and Miao--Tam conclusions. The same comparison also proves Ricci parallelism pointwise for solitons and quasi-Einstein manifolds.

title: Product and Quotient Set Dominance in Finite Groups
abstract: A classic problem in additive number theory asks whether a given subset of integers has more sums or differences. This inquiry naturally extends to finite groups, where one compares the sizes of the product set $AA$ and the quotient set $AA^{-1}$ for a subset $A \subseteq G$. A finite group is considered product-dominant if it contains a higher proportion of subsets where $|AA| > |AA^{-1}|$, and quotient-dominant if the reverse is true. We establish statistical criteria to determine the dominance behavior of large finite groups by analyzing the moments of the random variable $d(A) := |AA| - |AA^{-1}|$. By translating product and quotient relationships into graph-theoretic constructions, we compute these moments through counting independent sets. Our main result demonstrates that for a growing sequence of finite groups $G_k$ with center size $Z_k$ and involution count $T_k$, the condition $Z_k = o(T_k)$ implies the groups are eventually product-dominant. Conversely, if $T_k \cdot \sqrt{3}^{R_k/Z_k} = o(Z_k)$ (where $R_k$ denotes the number of elements whose square is central), the groups are eventually quotient-dominant. Using these asymptotic conditions, we resolve the Miller--Vissuet conjecture by proving that all dihedral groups $D_n$ for $n \geq 3$ are product-dominant. Furthermore, we classify the dominance behavior of several major families of groups, proving that symmetric groups and non-abelian finite simple groups are product-dominant, while groups of odd order and certain abelian groups are quotient-dominant. Finally, for groups that fall outside our asymptotic conditions, we derive an explicit formula for the first moment utilizing the irreducible characters and conjugacy classes of the group.

title: Numerical Smoothness and Error Analysis for Evolution Equations
abstract: This is a lecture note to introduce the innovative concept of numerical smoothness and its application in the error analysis of numerical solutions of evolution equations. We start from the two fundamentally different error splittings. One splitting is popular, which brings us to local error defined along the original solution and error propagation by numerical schemes. The well know Lax Equivalence Theorem is based on this error splitting. The other splitting can only be seen in a few numerical ODE books, which brings us to local error defined along the numerical solution and error propagation by the solutions of the evolution equations. The innovative concept of numerical smoothness arises from the second error splitting. While there are many difficulties when we use numerical stability in error analysis of nonlinear evolution equations, we will show that numerical smoothness works naturally in error analysis/estimation/control with advantages in several ways. We will define temporal and spatial numerical smoothness indicators, prove the necessity of the boundedness of these indicators for having optimal convergence rate, and show computable error estimates as functions of these smoothness indicators. Moreover, these error estimates are optimal in the approximatons' convergence rates and also optimal in the error propagation of the evolution equation. In comparison with error analysis framework of the Lax Equivalence Theorem, from the necessity results and the error estimates proven in the numerical smoothness framework, we have a new equivalence theory: Consistency + Numerical Smoothness <=> optimal error estimates. Unlike the Lax Equivalence Theorem, the new equivalence theory works well for nonlinear problems, nonlinear schemes, and many other complications of problems.

title: When Solvers Get Moody: Quantifying and Predicting Performance Variability in Mixed Integer Programming
abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers are widely used, yet their performance can vary substantially even under seemingly neutral perturbations. Such variability complicates benchmarking, and the interpretation of computational studies. We introduce the Weighted Variability Score (WVS), a robust multi-component metric that aggregates dispersion in normalized runtime, final optimality gap, LP iterations, and branch-and-bound nodes across repeated runs. On a large subset of MIPLIB 2017 instances, each solved in 100 randomized runs under a four-hour limit, WVS reveals a right-skewed distribution with a substantial upper tail: many instances are essentially stable, but some exhibit large variability that is not explained by basic properties alone. Notably, this experiment proved optimality for the open instance 'neos-5045105-creuse' in two SCIP runs. Using static descriptors and root-level features, a tree-based predictor with a gated tail uplift achieves a mean absolute error of 0.058 and Spearman rank correlation of 0.65 on a sealed test split. Feature-importance analysis highlights root degeneracy, matrix structure, coefficient ranges, and presolve reductions as the main drivers of high WVS. Because variability is systematic and partially predictable from inexpensive early-run features, our findings offer a practical tool for preemptive tuning and lay a foundation for fairer evaluation of new algorithms.

title: Existence of ergodic invariant measures for 3D Navier-Stokes eqs with superlinear noise
abstract: We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.

title: Recognizing oriented knots from finite quotients with one marked element
abstract: For an oriented tame knot $K$, let $G_K$ be its group, with positive meridian $μ_K$ and preferred longitude $λ_K$. We prove that the profinite completion $\widehat{G_K}$, marked by the conjugacy class of $μ_Kλ_K$, determines $K$ up to oriented equivalence. In fact, every isomorphism preserving this mark preserves the meridian and longitude with the same conjugator. The proof combines Xu's genuineness theorem with profinite JSJ theory and simultaneous boundary realization, and applies to satellite and composite knots. Consequently, Eisermann's colouring polynomials over all finite groups determine oriented knots.

title: Sums of Dirichlet eigenvalues in proximity of the disk and the ball
abstract: We derive second order perturbation expansions of volume-normalized sums of the first $n$ Dirichlet eigenvalues for near-circular and near-spherical domains. The disk (resp. ball) is only a critical shape when $n$ is the last index of an eigenvalue cluster, and in dimension two and three our expansions yield a finitely checkable criterion deciding whether the disk or ball is a weak local minimizer or a saddle point. In two dimensions, this allows us to show that there is an infinite number of cases in which the disk is a saddle point for finite eigenvalue sums.

title: Global Regular Solutions for One-Dimensional Degenerate Compressible Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Large Data and Far-Field Vacuum
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for a one-dimensional transverse-field isentropic non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system with viscosity $μ(ρ)=αρ^δ$, $0<δ\leq1$, and vacuum at spatial infinity. The viscosity therefore vanishes precisely where the density vanishes. We establish two global large-data theorems, one for the sublinear range $0<δ<1$ and one for the linear case $δ=1$, in a nontrivial invariant class of magnetic fields. The class is described by the frozen-in flux $h=b/ρ$ and its mass derivative $k=ρ^{-1}h_x$. The key identity $[\partial_t+u\partial_x,ρ^{-1}\partial_x]=0$ transports both $h$ and $k$, removes all negative powers of the density from the Lorentz force, and propagates the magnetic regularity. A modified effective-velocity entropy contains an additional coercive magnetic term, while its only error is controlled by $k$. Magnetic pressure also strengthens the density upper bound. These estimates close the large-data continuation argument in the ranges $0<δ<1$, $γ\geqδ+\tfrac12$, and $δ=1$, $γ>\tfrac32$. As a result, we extend the work of Cao, Li, and Zhu (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 2022) from the Navier-Stokes equations to the MHD equations.

title: Vector and matrix monotonicity characterisation of the "load forces" in nonlinear elasticity: compressible versus incompressible response
abstract: In this paper, we study the relation between different notions of monotonicity for isotropic hyperelastic compressible and incompressible materials. We study how to define the monotonicity concept on the manifold $\rm{Sym}^{++}(n)\cap \rm{SL}(n)$ of positive definite symmetric tensors with unit determinant and the corresponding spectral manifold $\mathcal S=\left\{(λ_1,\dotsc,λ_n)\in \mathbb{R}^n_+\,\middle|\, λ_1λ_2\cdotsλ_n=1\right\}$, and give a precise characterisation of monotonicity in the case of hyperelastic materials. In particular, we consider the monotonicity properties of the Biot stress tensor $T_{\rm Biot}(U)$, the engineering stress, or the load tensor.

title: Haar measure for totally positive split real semisimple quantum groups of classical type
abstract: Let $\hbar$ be a non-zero real number and put $q= e^{-πi \hbar}$. Let $G$ be a semisimple split real Lie group of classical type, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and associated Borel subalgebra $\mathfrak{b} \subseteq \mathfrak{g}$. We show that there exists a locally compact quantum group $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$ which integrates the Borel part $U_q(\mathfrak{b})$ of the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, viewed as a Hopf $*$-algebra. We further compute the associated Haar weights and modular data for $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$. Up to an excess Cartan part, the Drinfeld double of $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$ can be seen as an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup $G^+\subseteq G$.

title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^β\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, β> 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{é}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{ő}s--Tur{á}n--Koksma equidistribution.

title: Classification of can-Var diagrams of mixed Hodge structures and monodromic mixed Hodge modules on $\mathbb{C}$
abstract: By our previous work, the category of unipotent monodromic mixed Hodge modules on $\mathbb{C}$ is equivalent to the category of can-Var diagrams of mixed Hodge structures. In this paper, we show that the associated graded diagram with respect to the weight filtrations decomposes as a finite direct sum of four basic types tensored with pure Hodge structures, which we call a split graded model. We then show that every unipotent monodromic mixed Hodge module is represented by a split graded model together with a finite family of $\mathbb{C}$-linear maps. We also obtain an analogous description in the case where the monodromy has no eigenvalue $1$.

title: Qualitative-to-quantitative regularity for degenerate equations
abstract: We establish a principle that converts qualitative regularity into uniform interior estimates for degenerate equations. For the $p$-Laplace equation, $p>2$, we prove that local $C^{1,γ}$ regularity of every solution, without any uniform bound on the corresponding seminorms, implies uniform $C^{1,β}$ estimates for every $0<β<γ$. Thus, the optimal qualitative and quantitative gradient Hölder exponents coincide as suprema in every dimension. In the plane, this yields estimates controlled by the $L^p$ norm of the solution for every exponent below the sharp Iwaniec--Manfredi threshold. Applied to Xu's recent qualitative $C^{1,1/3}$ regularity for planar infinity-harmonic functions, we obtain uniform interior $C^{1,β}$ estimates for every $0<β<1/3$. For the nonlocal superconductivity equation $|Du|(-Δ)^s u=0$, with $1/2<s<1$, we prove that pointwise differentiability of all solutions with integrable tails implies uniform interior $C^{1,α}$ estimates for bounded solutions, for some $α>0$. The proofs combine compactness for shifted equations with an improvement-of-flatness iteration at variable scales.

title: Additive bases and the zero-sum invariant $\mathsf{N}(G)$ for groups $C_p\oplus C_{np}$
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer such that every regular sequence over $G$ of at least this length is an additive basis. Let $\mathsf N(G)$ be the least integer $l$ such that every weak-regular sequence $S$ over $G$ with $|S|\ge l$ has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence $T$ satisfying $\mathsf v_g(T)=\mathsf v_g(S)$ for some $g\mid S$. We obtain a common upper bound for $c_0(C_q\oplus C_{nq})$ for groups of odd order, where $q$ is prime, and prove $\mathsf N(G)\ge r(n_r-1)+1$ when $G=C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$. If $n\ge1$ and $p\ge3$ is the smallest prime divisor of $np$, we obtain $\mathsf N(C_p\oplus C_{np^2})=2np^2-1$ and give upper bounds for $\mathsf N(C_p\oplus C_{np})$ when $p\nmid n$. We also determine $\mathsf N(C_n)$ for two infinite families of cyclic groups arising in earlier work.

title: Isoperimetry of singular CMC hypersurfaces
abstract: We produce the first examples of singular isoperimetric boundaries with non-zero constant mean curvature in Riemannian manifolds. The main technical ingredient is establishing that, for constant mean curvature hypersurfaces containing isolated singularities modelled on strictly stable, strictly minimising regular tangent cones, weak strict stability implies local unique volume-constrained minimisation.

title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations with an application to elliptic boundary value problems
abstract: We establish a spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations on a Hilbert space. The proof relies on the Arens decomposition of a closed linear relation into an operator part and a purely multivalued part, reducing the problem directly to the classical spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators. No finite-dimensionality condition is imposed on the multivalued part. We also prove a finiterank approximation theorem for compact bounded linear relations and a Fredholm alternative for compact self-adjoint linear relations. As an application, we employ the theory of boundary triples to show that the inverse of the Neumann Laplacian on a bounded domain is a compact self-adjoint linear relation. The abstract spectral theorem then recovers the classical eigenfunction expansion of solutions to the Neumann problem: an L2-convergent series in terms of the non-constant Neumann eigenfunctions together with an arbitrary additive constant. The framework extends naturally to general elliptic boundary value problems with finite-dimensional kernel.

title: On the fault-tolerant metric dimension of maximal outerplanar graphs
abstract: Given a graph $G$, a set $W$ of vertices of $G$ is a resolving set if, for any pair of vertices $z_1$ and $z_2$ of $G$, there is a vertex $w\in W$ such that $d(w,z_1)\ne d(w,z_2)$, where $d(u,v)$ denotes the length of a shortest path between the vertices $u$ and $v$. The metric dimension of a graph $G$, $β(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a resolving set of $G$. A resolving set $W$ is fault-tolerant if $W\setminus \{w\}$ is a resolving set for any $w\in W$. The fault-tolerant metric dimension of a graph $G$, denoted by $β'(G)$, is the minimum cardinality of a fault-tolerant resolving set of $G$. In this paper, we study the fault-tolerant metric dimension problem in maximal outerplanar graphs. In particular, we show that there are exactly two maximal outerplanar graphs with $β'(G)=3$. We also show that $4\le β'(G) \le 6$ for any maximal outerplanar graph $G$ of order at least 7 and metric dimension 2. Moreover, we establish the upper bound $β'(G) \le \left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$ for maximal outerplanar graphs $G$ of order $n\ge 5$, by building in linear time a fault-tolerant resolving set of cardinality $\left\lceil \frac{2n}{3} \right\rceil$.

title: On $p$-groups with one nonlinear codegree
abstract: For an irreducible character $χ$ of a finite group $G$, its codegree is defined by $cod(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$. In this paper, we characterize fnite $p$-groups whose nonlinear irreducible characters all have the same codegree.

title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
abstract: We show the convergence of a commonly used mesh-free discretization of a dynamic non-linear bond-based peridynamic model with irreversible damage implemented via a bond-breakage criterion for a fixed horizon $δ>0$. The model chosen here is a mathematically well-posed regularization of a discontinuous peridynamic operator often found in the literature, which assumes that fracture results from strain in tension only. We explicitly include the one-point quadrature used in this scheme in the analysis. The convergence is with respect to the natural norm of the solution space given by $C^1([0,T],L^\infty(Ω)^d)$, and therefore $L^\infty(Ω)^d$ in the spatial coordinates. This result heavily constrains the spatial regularity of the continuous solution which we prove afterwards. More specifically, for locally $L$-Lipschitz continuous input data, local Lipschitz bounds are derived for the displacement, regardless of damage. This is consistent with interpreting the peridynamic model used here as an approximation to a truly discontinuous fracture model with a length-scale parameter given by the horizon $δ>0$. We note that we do not deal with the limit of the solutions as $δ\searrow 0$.

title: Thurston's Legacy at the Interface of Surface Dynamics, Train Tracks, and Arithmetic
abstract: In this chapter, we discuss the interaction between low-dimensional dynamics, symbolic dynamics, and geometric topology, focusing on the algebraic characterization and asymptotic behaviour of stretch factors or equivalently pseudo-Anosov dilatations. We first review the algebraic foundations linking Perron--Frobenius theory, multi-variable Euclidean algorithms, and Lind's characterization of topological entropy for shifts of finite type, emphasizing recent constraints on the Perron--Frobenius degree of expansion constants. We then relate these dynamical invariants to the combinatorial world, examining train tracks for surfaces and automorphisms of free groups. Finally, we briefly review the relevance of fibered 3-manifolds, detailing how the Thurston norm, Fried's concavity theorem over fibered cones, and McMullen's Teichmüller polynomial come into play.

title: Loss of derivatives for hyperbolic operators with coefficients oscillating in time
abstract: We consider second-order strictly hyperbolic operators whose coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in space and may oscillate near the initial time. Their first two time derivatives are bounded by the corresponding powers of $\frac{1}{t}(\log\frac{1}{t})^α$ with $0\leqslantα<1$, and the first time derivative satisfies the corresponding spatial Lipschitz bound. By combining Tarama's energy with frequency-dependent weights, we prove an energy estimate without loss for $α=0$ and with a stretched logarithmic upper bound for the loss when $0<α<1$, which implies an arbitrarily small loss in the Sobolev scale. These estimates extend the analysis of Colombini, Del Santo and Fanelli [\emph{Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa Cl. Sci. (5)} \textbf{26} (2025)] for spatially Lipschitz coefficients to time-derivative bounds with an additional logarithmic factor.

title: Optimal Control of Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes with Variable Time
abstract: The paper is devoted to a broad class of optimal control problems governed by constrained sweeping processes with controlled dynamics, controlled prox-regular moving sets, and variable time included in the optimization process. Employing an advanced version of the method of discrete approximations, we verify its well-posedness with appropriate strong convergence of feasible and optimal solutions. This approach leads us to considering a parametric family of discrete-time controlled sweeping processes, which are reduced in turn to nondynamic mathematical programs with special types of geometric and functional constraints. Invoking powerful tools of first-order and second-order variational analysis and generalized differentiation, we derive necessary optimality conditions for discrete-time and then---by passing to the limit over the diminishing step of discretization---continuous-time controlled sweeping processes. A crucial role in our device is played by explicit coderivative evaluations of set-valued mapping associated with the sweeping dynamics. In this way, we establish novel necessary optimality conditions for local minimizers of continuous-time controlled sweeping processes that contain absolutely continuous and BV adjoint arcs, local and global maximization conditions, $L^2$ active set multipliers, vector measures generated by sweeping and control constraints, and free-time transversality condition expressed through the averaged Hamiltonian. For suitably selected multipliers, we also obtain nondegenerate forms of these conditions when the optimal trajectory starts on the boundary of the moving set. The efficiency of the obtained results is illustrated by some examples related to practical modeling.

title: Higher-Order Gaussian Approximations on Path Space for the Simple Symmetric Exclusion Process
abstract:
Quantitative Gaussian approximation estimates on path space are established for the nonequilibrium density fluctuations of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) on a $d$-dimensional discrete torus of mesh size $1/n$, started from a product measure with a smooth density profile. A novel $n$-dependent modified Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is constructed that incorporates higher-order lattice information while remaining linear and Gaussian. It is shown that, for sufficiently high modification orders, this modification yields quantitative Gaussian approximation error bounds of order $n^{-\min\{d/2,2\}}$ for a class of smooth functionals of the entire fluctuation trajectory. In addition, it is shown that retaining an explicit microscopic correlation correction leaves a remainder of order $n^{-d/2}$, thereby distinguishing contributions to the bound due to correlations from those due to spatial approximation. For nonconstant initial profiles in dimensions $d\ge3$, a separate argument yields matching upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-2}$ for the direct weak error of suitable quadratic test functionals, provided that the modification orders are sufficiently high.
  The proof is based on a novel path-dependent Trotter formula. Its derivation builds on the introduction of a concept of horizontal absolute continuity for non-anticipative functionals and a corresponding martingale formula for Markov jump processes. This formula is subsequently combined with an integral backward Kolmogorov equation for Gaussian continuation functionals. A second ingredient of the proof is a refinement of the exchangeable-pair argument introduced by the authors in a previous work, thereby improving the central-limit rate $n^{-\min\{d/2,1\}}$ to $n^{-d/2}$ for the initial empirical fluctuations.

title: Higher mod $p$ Satake transforms: explicit formulas and images for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
abstract:
Heyer's left adjoint to derived parabolic induction gives rise to higher mod $p$ Satake transforms \[ \mathcal S_V^i: \mathcal H_G(V) \longrightarrow \mathcal H_M\bigl(H^i(K_U,V)\bigr), \] whose extreme degrees recover Herzig's invariant and coinvariant transforms. For $G=\mathbf G(F)$, where $\mathbf G$ is a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$, we describe these maps explicitly using Mackey decompositions and corestriction in group cohomology. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, we evaluate them on the standard Hecke generators, showing that their support lies in a single Weyl orbit and that their values on the individual support cosets are concrete corestriction operators.
  For $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, we determine the image in every cohomological degree for each non-Steinberg Serre weight. The endpoint images are the classical polynomial Satake images, while every interior image is of the form \[ k[x,y^{\pm1}]/(x^r) \] for some positive integer $r$. Thus, every interior image is a finite nilpotent thickening of the Laurent polynomial algebra $k[y^{\pm1}]$. We give explicit bounds for its thickness, prove that they are sharp, and show that in the unramified case every interior image is either reduced or a square-zero thickening.

title: Tight Guarantees for Static Policies in Vehicle Sharing Networks
abstract:
We study pricing in a vehicle sharing network with $N$ locations and $C$ vehicles, motivated by on-demand bike, scooter, and car sharing, as well as robotaxi and ride sharing services. Customers request directed trips between locations, with travel times following general distributions, and leave without service if no vehicle is available. Pricing affects both demand for trips and the distribution of vehicles across locations.
