abstract: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

title: An Infinite Family of Apéry-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
abstract:
Euler's constant $γ$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Apéry-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce.
  We present a novel identity that expresses $γ$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Apéry-like approximations of $γ$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.

title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
abstract: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers. Regarding the connection between the clique and coloring parameters of graph powers, we propose a spectral analogue of Wegner's conjecture, determine the extremal values for graph squares, and establish the conjecture for all powers when the spectral-radius bound is sufficiently small. Finally, we connect our spectral polynomial method with coding theory: we prove that for distance-regular graphs, optimisation over the adjacency algebra recovers Delsarte's linear programming bound for anticodes.

title: Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces in rearrangement-invariant and Hardy spaces
abstract: In 1981, Bourgain, Rosenthal, and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$. We extend their construction to rearrangement-invariant spaces and Hardy spaces. For any separable rearrangement-invariant space $X$ with non-trivial Boyd indices, we show that these subspaces are complemented, previously obtained by Ghawadrah via a different argument, and establish the following dichotomy: Either one can extract an uncountable family of pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces, or they are all isomorphic to $X$. To this end, we introduce an ordinal index that detects whether $X$ embeds complementably into an arbitrary separable Banach space. On the other hand, we give sufficient conditions which imply that in certain spaces close to $L_1$ and $H^1$, these subspaces fail to be complemented.

title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
abstract:
The expressivity of a neural network $Φ$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $β(Φ^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $β(Φ(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d
  } β_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}β_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($β_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.

title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
abstract: The main result is an obstruction to the presence of contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension. As a first application, we prove a 5-dimensional analogue (under stronger assumptions) of a Reeb stability theorem for confoliations in dimension 3 due to Eliashberg and Thurston. Refining work of the first author with Cardona, we further give two new notions of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension generalizing the 3-dimensional notion of Eliashberg-Thurston. As a second application of our main theorem, we then give an example, in any ambient odd dimension, of a c-symplectic (and in fact strong symplectic) foliation that cannot be contact approximated, in either of these two senses. This relies on the property, of independent interest, that contact structures approximating (in these senses) a weakly c-symplectic confoliation are also weakly fillable. The proofs of all these statements rely on pseudo-holomorphic curve theory. Lastly, we describe several natural classes of examples of these types of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations.

title: Markov Chain Convergence in Kernel-Induced Geometry
abstract: We study the convergence of Markov chains in the geometry induced by Hilbertian embeddings associated with positive definite kernels, also called Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). Under a contraction assumption in the kernel-induced geometry, and a standard spectral gap assumption, we establish non-asymptotic, high-probability bounds for the convergence of the empirical occupation measure to the invariant measure. The obtained bounds separate the roles of the two conditions: the spectral gap determines the effective sample size in the leading term, while the kernel contraction enters only through a linear correction. As an application, we study one-step prediction of dynamical systems from a single trajectory, deriving fast learning rates for a nonlinear least-squares estimator. The rates highlight the interplay between mixing properties in the kernel-induced geometry and the classical source and capacity conditions used in the analysis of least-squares.

title: Heterogeneous Demand-Private Coded Caching: Exact Characterization for Two Users and Two Files
abstract: We consider the demand-private coded caching problem with heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities, where each user must recover its requested file without learning any information about the demands of the other users. We first extend the virtual-user reduction technique to accommodate heterogeneous cache sizes, thereby enabling the construction of demand-private coded caching schemes from non-private schemes. Our main contribution is an exact characterization of the memory-rate trade-off for the fundamental setting of two users and two files with arbitrary file sizes and cache capacities. Specifically, we characterize the optimal trade-off through eight linear inequalities and establish achievability by constructing explicit coded caching schemes for the non-trivial corner points, followed by memory sharing. These constructions include novel asymmetric cache placement strategies tailored to heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities. For the converse, we exploit the distributional equivalences induced by demand privacy to derive information-theoretic lower bounds that explicitly account for the underlying heterogeneity. Our results generalize the exact memory-rate trade-off characterization for the homogeneous demand-private coded caching setting with two users and two files, while quantifying the additional transmission cost imposed by demand privacy compared with the non-private heterogeneous setting.

title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

title: Unifying spherical convolutions through lifting
abstract: We develop a unified description of convolution on the sphere by lifting to the rotation group. A number of definitions of spherical convolution have been proposed, differing in whether the kernel is axisymmetric or directional, whether the output is on the sphere or the rotation group, whether the signals carry spin, and in their computational cost. No unified treatment exists. Regarding the sphere as the homogeneous space $S^2 \cong \text{SO(3)}/\text{SO(2)}$, we lift a spin $s$ field to the rotation group, convolve on $\text{SO(3)}$, and project back to the sphere through the adjoint of the lift for a potentially different spin $s'$. We recover every rotation-equivariant convolution considered previously through constraints on the kernel, spin choices and inclusion or omission of the lift and projection. For maps between fields of fixed input and output spin, we prove that directional kernels, output on the sphere and equivariance cannot be achieved simultaneously. We make explicit that spin fields are sections of associated line bundles, linking the physics and bundle literatures, and express the spin rotation phase as the character of the twist of the section. We present harmonic-space algorithms for the exact and efficient computation of lifted spherical convolutions of band-limited fields by appealing to sampling theorems on the sphere and rotation group. All operators are implemented in the open-source s2conv code, and numerical experiments confirm the reductions and the equivariance of the operators to machine precision. Finally, we illustrate the operators on fields measured on the Earth and on the celestial sky.

title: Interacting Stochastic Systems with Agent-Based Sampling and Connection-Based Reinforcement
abstract:
We introduce a general class of interacting reinforced stochastic systems evolving on a network. The dynamics are governed by two distinct interaction structures: a sampling network, which determines how information is acquired, and a reinforcement network, which determines how the sampled information influences future evolution. Processes generate Bernoulli observations through preferential, de-preferential, or mixed sampling, while observations are transmitted through an edge-dependent affine reinforcement mechanism.
  We formulate the dynamics as a stochastic approximation scheme and study their asymptotic behaviour. We establish sufficient conditions for almost sure convergence to a deterministic limit and, when the sampling and reinforcement graphs coincide, derive graph-theoretic criteria involving odd cycles, mixed-sampling vertices, and subcritical reinforcement. Under additional structural assumptions, we establish almost sure convergence and partial synchronization in a random-limit regime. In the deterministic regime, we also prove a law of the iterated logarithm and a central limit theorem under suitable spectral and regularity conditions. Finally, we show how the framework encompasses interacting urn models with edge-dependent reinforcement, urns with memory, and random walks with memory.

title: Existence and large-field asymptotics of Hopfions in a continuum model of frustrated magnets
abstract: We study a continuum model of frustrated magnetism that supports particle-like field configurations with nontrivial Hopf index. The energy functional combines competing second and first order exchange interactions with a stabilizing external magnetic field and gives rise to a variational problem for maps from three-dimensional space into the two-sphere. We prove the existence of energy minimizers in infinitely many nontrivial homotopy classes. We further establish the existence of a unit-charge Hopfion in the regime of strong external fields. Finally, we analyze the corresponding large-field limit, identify the natural concentration scale, and prove strong convergence of suitably rescaled minimizers to a minimizer of a limiting variational problem.

title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
abstract: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
abstract: In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.

title: Counterexamples to Minkowski-type inequalities and the Rees converse for modules via mixed Buchsbaum-Rim Multiplicities
abstract: In this paper, we explore mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities of finite-colength submodules of free modules over Noetherian local rings. We extend the Hilbert-polynomial construction to submodules in arbitrary homogeneous degrees and prove a product formula for the resulting coefficients. We then examine module analogues of Teissier's coefficient inequalities and the Minkowski inequality. Explicit examples show that the coefficientwise power inequalities, log-convexity, and the product-root inequality can all fail; several failures occur over regular local rings. We also prove that equality of integral closures forces equality of all mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities, while a one-dimensional example shows that the converse fails for arbitrary modules. A converse is recovered when the module closures are the integral closures of modules of the form $IF$ for $\mathfrak m$-primary ideals $I$. The general converse problem in dimension at least two is stated at the end.

title: Best proximity point results of operator type condensing mappings via measure of noncompactness and application to an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$
abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncompactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.

title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
abstract: We formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture. The public Lean declaration is reproduced in this paper. Its geometric interpretation follows, and verification is recorded in 4.

title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
abstract: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in $R^3$ with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of two strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains two closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from the periodic solution of a Riccati equation.

title: An Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients
abstract: We give an exposition of a proof, discovered by Astra, of an Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients. We explain this method in the simpler elliptic and parabolic settings as well.

title: Property $R_\infty$ for Artin and Coxeter groups whose outer automorphisms are length-preserving
abstract: We prove that every length-preserving automorphism of a nonspherical Artin or Coxeter group has infinite Reidemeister number. As a consequence, we establish property $R_\infty$ for large-type free-of-infinity Artin groups, infinite strongly rigid Coxeter groups, and infinite virtually abelian Coxeter groups, including all affine Coxeter groups. We also prove that the automorphism group of every infinite irreducible non-affine strongly rigid Coxeter group is acylindrically hyperbolic.

title: The Inviscid Limit in Uniformly Local Yudovich Spaces
abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes and Euler equations with the velocity in $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and the vorticity in the uniformly local Yudovich space $Y^θ_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $θ$ grows sufficiently slowly, then for every $T>0$, solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation converge to solutions of the Euler equation in $L^{\infty}([0,T];L^2_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ as $ν\to 0^+$, provided they are generated from the same initial data.

title: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
abstract: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.

title: Characterizing higher-dimensional Hölder domains via spherical geometric functions
abstract:
In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has Hölder decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,β}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold.
  Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $β$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.

title: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
abstract: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.

title: Fast and Stable Arbitrary Precision Approximate Matrix Multiplication
abstract: We present several new and surprising results on the theory and practice of Arbitrary Precision Approximate (APA) matrix multiplication, which refers to algorithms that output merely approximations to matrix multiplication even in exact arithmetic. While APA algorithms have been around for nearly half a century, and despite the fact that they have potentially lower (asymptotic) cost than many fast exact matrix multiplication schemes, they have not been studied as closely, to the extent that relatively little is known about their numerical properties. In this paper, we shine a spotlight on these algorithms by presenting three important results. First, we provide a new search algorithm for APA routines that is easy to use, automatically generates encoding matrices with functional entries, and can match or beat the best known APA algorithms for several sizes. In particular, we improve the upper bound on the border rank of $\langle 2,4,5 \rangle$ matrix multiplication. Second, we combine this insight with alternative bases to minimize the number of additions in an APA algorithm, thereby improving its leading coefficient. Finally, we prove the same kind of stability that characterizes fast exact matrix multiplication for an algorithm of Bini [Calcolo 1980] that computes an exact product of two matrices using a modified APA scheme (with or without alternative bases).

title: A Riesz-Map Preconditioned Extragradient Method for Price Formation in Mean Field Games
abstract: We develop and analyze a projected extragradient method, preconditioned by a Riesz map, for a first-order price-formation mean field game in one space dimension. The model couples Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and transport equations through a global market-clearing constraint. Finite propagation justifies truncating the first-order transport equation to a bounded interval. A monotone weak formulation incorporates the mixed initial--terminal data. Its Riesz map uses $L^2$ norms for density and price directions and a space-time $H^1$ norm for value-function directions, preconditioning the residual without adding higher-order regularization terms to the MFG equations. A density-only argument rules out cocoercivity on the localized admissible set in every equivalent Hilbert metric, motivating extragradient updates. For $H(x,p)=p^2/2$, we use a monotone upwind discretization with adjoint-consistent transport and a state-constraint boundary closure. We establish a mesh-independent Lipschitz bound on bounded convex admissible sets with uniform density, slope, and price bounds. With exact metric projection onto these sets, the iteration converges to a solution of the discrete variational inequality on each fixed grid, with an admissible step-size threshold independent of both mesh sizes. Convergence under mesh refinement is not proved. On a quadratic benchmark, all reported runs reach the stopping tolerance with one fixed step size across a factor-of-16 reduction in both mesh sizes. Price errors and value-function errors measured away from low-density regions decay approximately at first order under refinement, while density errors decrease more slowly.

title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
abstract: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight strong-generation induction and $C_2$-cofiniteness, semisimple descent for a full corner of Zhu's algebra, modular Galois symmetry, and holomorphic $E_8$ extensions.

title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
abstract: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.

title: On diagonal sections of Markov products of copulas
abstract: Given a bivariate copula $C$, the bivariate copula $Ψ(C)$ is defined as the Markov product of $C^T$ and $C$. In this paper we consider the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$ under the additional assumption that its value at a single point is known. We determine the exact upper and lower bounds for the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$, given that $Ψ(C)(a,a)=d \in [a^2,a]$, where $a \in [0,1]$ is a fixed point. Furthermore, we describe some additional properties of the transformation $Ψ$, such as its behavior under ordinal sums and the survival operation. We also study checkerboard copulas in the range of $Ψ$ and matrices associated to them.
